chunks.title: Compression
chunks.heading: Compare with and without
chunks.text:
Two request headers let you measure it on one request:

```bash
# Baseline: every boon off
curl -si http://localhost/v1/chat/completions -H "x-obleth-boons: off" ...

# Lossy forced on for this request
curl -si http://localhost/v1/chat/completions -H "x-obleth-boons: lossy" ...
```

`lossy` turns the lossy pass on even where the tenant hasn't; the model must still hold the boon. Whenever compression ran, the response says what it did:

```text
x-obleth-compression: before=18423;after=11278;saved=7145
```

[`obench compression`](/docs/operate/benchmarks) runs this comparison across sample payloads.

chunks.title: Compression
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Nothing extra; the neural sidecar is optional
  Settings › Boons › Compression, then the model's page › Boons
  No helper calls; it lowers the tokens the model is billed for

Compression runs before the request goes to the model's backend, so the savings cut the input tokens billed and the time to first token. It makes no model calls of its own.

chunks.title: Compression
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compression on | `compression_enabled` | `false` |
| Code compaction | `compression_code_compaction` | `false` |
| Cross-turn dedup | `compression_dedup` | `false` |
| Log compaction | `compression_compact_logs` | `false` |
| Lossy | `compression_allow_lossy` | `false` |
| Smallest input | `compression_min_tokens` | `128` tokens |
| Pieces | `compression_max_segments` | `64` segments per request for JSON and code |
| Lossy pieces | `compression_max_lossy_segments` | `4` segments per request for lossy prose |
| Originals kept | `compression_original_ttl_secs` | `3600` s |
| Prose kept | `compression_neural_keep_ratio` | `0.5` of sentences, above 0 up to 1 |

A `0`, or a **Prose kept** outside its range, keeps the stored value.

Whatever the settings, the JSON and code pass reads at most 8 MB of a request's text. A piece that would go past that is sent as it is.

By default the lossy pass ranks sentences with a built-in heuristic (length, density and overlap with the question). The **compressor** sidecar ranks them with a trained extractive model instead, served on CPU in a container you run, so no text leaves your infrastructure. The gateway still splits sentences, picks what to keep and stores the original; the sidecar only scores. It makes one call per request with as many sentences as a pod can score within the gateway's timeout (`OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_TIMEOUT_MS`, about 30 a second), and on a timeout or any error the h

chunks.title: Compression
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Open **Settings › Boons** and switch **Compression** on. With nothing else set, it only compacts JSON, which is lossless. **Open** the row to add more under **What it does**: **Code compaction**, **Log compaction**, **Cross-turn dedup** and **Lossy**. These are the defaults for every tenant that has no settings of its own. Save with the save bar.

On the model's page, switch **Compression** on under **Boons** and save.

On a tenant's page, under **Compression**, switch on **Its own compression settings**. Then set **Compression** on or off for that tenant, and each of **Code compaction**, **Cross-turn dedup**, **Log compaction** and **Allow lossy**. Switch it off again to follow the gateway's defaults.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "compression_enabled": true, "compression_dedup": true, "compression_compact_logs": true }'

curl -X PATCH http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants/$TENANT_ID/compression \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "policy": { "enabled": true, "code_compaction": true, "dedup": true, "compact_logs": true, "allow_lossy": false } }'
```

Send `{ "policy": null }` to clear a tenant's settings.

chunks.title: Compression
chunks.heading: What each pass does
chunks.text:
| Pass | What changes | Lossless? | On by default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **JSON** | An array of similar objects becomes an `OBLETH_TABLE` (a header plus CSV rows); other JSON is minified. Each rewrite is checked to reconstruct the original. | Yes | Yes, whenever the boon runs |
| **Code compaction** | Trailing whitespace stripped and runs of blank lines collapsed in fenced code | Whitespace only | No |
| **Cross-turn dedup** | A large block repeated across messages becomes a `[ref:HASH]` marker | The original is kept to retrieve | No |
| **Log compaction** | Repeated log lines collapse to one line with a count; errors and warnings stay | Near-lossless | No |
| **Lossy** | Long prose keeps its most important sentences, with a note of how many were left out | No; extractive, never rewritten | No |

Every pass skips segments under **Smallest input** tokens and a segment that wouldn't get smaller. JSON and code compaction cover every message, tool output included. Dedup, log compaction and lossy leave the active turn alone, which is the latest user message and a trailing assistant message, and they take turns: a segment one of them replaced is not offered to the next. Each replaces at most **Lossy pieces** segments per request. Lossy keeps any sentence that shares a word of four letters or more with the latest user message. It compacts a segment once, on the turn it first appears, and keeps that form in Redis for **Originals kept**. Later turns get the same form again, so

chunks.title: Compression
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
Compacted segments in place of the originals: `OBLETH_TABLE` blocks, `[ref:HASH]` markers, collapsed log lines and shortened prose. When dedup, log compaction or lossy replaced something, the original is kept in Redis for **Originals kept**, per tenant. If the model has function calling and the [tool loop](/docs/boons/tool-loop) is on, the gateway also adds a `retrieve_original` tool and a short note, so the model can fetch the full text by its hash. The gateway answers that call itself from Redis; it never reaches the backend or the client. An expired or unknown hash returns a "no longer available" message.

Without function calling or the tool loop, compaction still happens; only the tool is left out.

chunks.title: Image generation
chunks.heading: Ask for a picture
chunks.text:
```bash
curl http://localhost/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5-3",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Draw a lighthouse at dusk in flat vector style."}]
  }'
```

The model calls `generate_image`, the gateway runs it, and the final assistant message ends with the picture as a markdown image with a data URL:

```text
Here is your lighthouse at dusk.

![a lighthouse at dusk, flat vector style, warm orange sky…](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo...)
```

This works on streaming and non-streaming requests, and the response carries `x-obleth-boons: image_generation`.

chunks.title: Image generation
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A registered `image` model and a chat model with function calling
  Settings › Boons › Image generation, then the model's page › Boons
  The image model's price per image, billed as `image_generation_boon`

chunks.title: Image generation
chunks.heading: Replayed images
chunks.text:
When a client sends an earlier reply back as history, the gateway replaces each image it attached with a receipt of the call that made it:

```text
[image rendered by generate_image(prompt="a lighthouse at dusk…") and shown to the user]
```

So a conversation doesn't grow by megabytes per picture, and a follow-up such as "now make it night" calls the tool again instead of describing an image in words. This runs on every chat request, whether or not the model holds the boon, because it only removes what the gateway inserted. `x-obleth-boons: off` skips it.

chunks.title: Image generation
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image generation on | `image_generation_enabled` | `false` |
| Image model | `image_generation_model` | none; `""` clears it, which turns the boon off |
| Allowed sizes | `image_generation_allowed_sizes` | `512x512`, `1024x1024`; an empty list puts the default back |
| Images per call | `image_generation_max_images_per_request` | `2`, clamped to `1`–`4`; `0` keeps the stored value |
| Image timeout | `image_generation_timeout_ms` | `120000` ms, per generation |
| Tool description | `image_generation_tool_description` | built-in text; `""` puts the default back |

The tool is added when Image generation is on in Settings with an image model picked, the model has `image_generation` in its `boons` list, and the model is flagged `supports_function_calling`. Without function calling the model gets no tool and the gateway logs a warning; the model's page marks the boon as doing nothing, and **Settings › Needs you** lists the model.

If the client already defines a tool named `generate_image`, or a granted MCP server exposes one, that tool wins and the boon is inactive for the request.

A model can hold both this boon and [speculation](/docs/boons/speculation). When the speculation classifier can't place a request in a category, speculation abstains so the model can draw.

- A size outside **Allowed sizes** is replaced with the first allowed size.
- **Images per call** is also the total for the whole request; a call past it

chunks.title: Image generation
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Add a model of type `image` that serves an OpenAI-compatible `/images/generations` endpoint, and set its price per image. See [Images, audio and speech](/docs/clients/multi-modal-models).

Open **Settings › Boons**, switch **Image generation** on and **Open** its row. Pick the **Image model**, then set **Images per call**, **Image timeout** and **Allowed sizes** under **Limits**. Save with the save bar.

On the chat model's page, turn on **Function calling** under **Native**, then switch **Image generation** on under **Boons** and save. The model calls the tool itself, so the switch can't be turned on while Function calling is off, and turning Function calling off turns it off.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "image_generation_enabled": true,
    "image_generation_model": "flux-schnell",
    "image_generation_allowed_sizes": ["512x512", "1024x1024"],
    "image_generation_max_images_per_request": 2,
    "image_generation_timeout_ms": 120000
  }'
```

The Tool loop switch doesn't need to be on; image generation works without it.

chunks.title: Image generation
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
- A `generate_image` tool with `prompt`, `size` (one of the **Allowed sizes**) and `n` (up to **Images per call**), described by the **Tool description**.
- For a client that sent no tools and has no tool-loop nudge, a short system note: the tool exists, call it when the user wants a picture, and don't offer it otherwise.
- After the call, a short text receipt instead of the image, such as `Generated 1 image (1024x1024) for prompt "a lighthouse at dusk…"`. The image travels separately and is attached to the final reply, so its bytes never enter the model's context.
- On failure, a receipt saying the image could not be generated and why. The model then tells the user in prose.

chunks.title: Knowledge
chunks.heading: A request where it helps
chunks.text:
```bash
curl http://localhost/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5-3",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "How many credits can a student transfer in?"}]
  }'
```

When passages were added, the response carries `x-obleth-boons: knowledge`.

chunks.title: Knowledge
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A registered embedding model and some `.txt`, `.md` or `.csv` files
  Knowledge › Retrieval settings, then attach a collection to a model
  Nothing billed; query embeddings are free to the tenant

You upload files into **collections**. The gateway splits each document into chunks and embeds them with the collection's embedding model. For a model that has the Knowledge boon and at least one attached collection, it embeds the user's question, finds the best-scoring chunks, and places them ahead of the conversation. Retrieval runs from an in-process index inside the gateway; the request path never queries Postgres.

chunks.title: Knowledge
chunks.heading: Retrieval settings
chunks.text:
These live on **Knowledge › Retrieval settings** and apply to every model. A profile sets the first four:

| Profile | Chunks per question | Minimum score | Token budget | Question from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Standard** (default) | 5 | 0.35 | 1500 | 2 turns |
| **Precise** | 3 | 0.5 | 800 | 1 turn |
| **Broad** | 10 | 0.25 | 4000 | 4 turns |

| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retrieval | `enabled` | `false` |
| Chunks per question | `top_k` | `5` |
| Minimum score | `min_score` | `0.35`, cosine similarity from 0 to 1 |
| Token budget | `max_context_tokens` | `1500` |
| Question from | `query_turns` | `2` |
| Embedding timeout | `embed_timeout_ms` | `1500` ms |
| Query cache | `query_cache_ttl_s` | `600` s |
| Largest upload | `max_upload_bytes` | 10 MiB per file, at most 50 MiB |
| Chunks per collection | `max_chunks_per_collection` | `100000` |
| Index batch | `index_batch_size` | `32` chunks per embedding call; halved for the rest of a document when the embedder refuses a batch as overloaded |
| Index timeout | `index_timeout_ms` | `30000` ms |
| Stale after | `index_stale_after_secs` | `1800` s |
| Keep chunk text in traces | `debug_snapshot` | `false` |

Through the Management API, send only what you want to change; an omitted field, a `0`, or a `min_score` outside 0 to 1 keeps the stored value:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/knowledge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: applicatio

chunks.title: Knowledge
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Open **Knowledge** and choose **New collection**. Give it a name, an optional description and the **Embedding model**. Names are unique. Register an embedding model on the Models page first if you have none.

On the collection's page (`/knowledge/<name>`), upload files under **Documents**. Each moves from Queued to Indexing to Indexed, or to Failed with the error shown; failures are listed first.

Under **Used by**, pick a chat model and choose **Attach**. Attaching grants that model the Knowledge boon. You can also switch **Knowledge** on under a model's **Boons** and pick its collections there.

On the Knowledge page, choose **Turn retrieval on**, or open the **Retrieval settings** tab and switch **Retrieval** on. Pick a profile and save.

On the collection's page, type a question under **Try a search**. It shows the chunks that match, their scores, and which would be handed to the model under the current settings.

chunks.title: Knowledge
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
The passages arrive in a `<knowledge>` block with a short instruction to use them only when they are relevant. It is appended to the system message, or becomes one; for a model flagged as not supporting system messages, it is put at the start of the latest user message.

The query is the last **Question from** user messages, newest first, cut to 2,000 characters. It is captured before [compression](/docs/boons/compression) and the block is added after compression and after the tenant's input [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails), so the query is the user's own words and the passages reach the model unchanged. A follow-up turn in the [tool loop](/docs/boons/tool-loop) carries the same block.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: Boons compose per request
chunks.text:
A model can hold several boons. For each chat request the gateway applies them in a fixed order, and each one runs only if the request calls for it:

1. Vision describes any images.
2. Knowledge captures the retrieval query from the user's own words.
3. Compression compacts JSON and code.
4. The tool loop, image generation and web search add their tools.
5. Compression's dedup, log and lossy passes run.
6. Structured output arms its schema.
7. The tenant's input guardrails scan the request.
8. Knowledge injects the retrieved passages.
9. Speculation decides whether to draft.

Speculation is the only boon that steps aside for others: structured output, output guardrails and a tool loop with real MCP tools all need the model's own answer.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: Fail-open
chunks.text: A boon never fails a request. No helper model, an upstream error, a timeout or a reply that can't be parsed leaves the request or response as it was, and the model answers on its own. When something was skipped that the client might care about, the response carries `x-obleth-boons-warning`, for example `structured_output_validation_failed`.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: Helper calls and billing
chunks.text:
Boons that call another model (the vision describer, the structured-output fixer, tool-loop turns, the speculation drafter and verifier, the image model) or a search tool record that call as its own usage row against the calling tenant and key. Each row has `admission = boon`, a `request_type` naming the boon, and the id of the request it served as `parent_request_id`, so the request's panel in Request logs lists it under **Helper calls**:

| Boon | `request_type` |
| --- | --- |
| Vision | `vision_boon` |
| Structured output | `structured_output_boon` |
| Tool loop | `tool_loop` |
| Image generation | `image_generation_boon` |
| Web search | `web_search_boon`, with no tokens and no cost |
| Speculation | `speculation_draft`, `speculation_verify` |
| Guardrails (guard model) | `guardrails_boon` |

Helper spend counts toward the tenant's and key's [term budgets](/docs/sharing/quotas-and-rate-limits), so a tenant at its cap can't keep spending through boons. Playground and benchmark tenants have their helper rows labelled `benchmark`, like their other requests. Knowledge's query embeddings and compression are not billed.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Chat models you grant a boon to
  Settings › Boons, then the model's page › Boons
  Helper-model calls, billed to the caller's tenant

A boon is an ability the gateway adds to a model: seeing images, answering in a JSON schema, calling tools, drawing, searching the web, quoting your documents. The gateway does the extra work around the model's own call, so clients send ordinary requests and need no changes.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: The boons
chunks.text:
| Boon | What it adds | Model's `boons` value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Vision](/docs/boons/vision) | A describer model turns images into text for a text-only model | `vision` |
| [Structured output](/docs/boons/structured-output) | Replies held to a `response_format` JSON schema, repaired when they break it | `structured_output` |
| [Tool loop](/docs/boons/tool-loop) | The gateway runs a model's calls to registered MCP tools and feeds back the results | none: granted through the model's tool servers |
| [Image generation](/docs/boons/image-generation) | A `generate_image` tool backed by a registered image model | `image_generation` |
| [Web search](/docs/boons/web-search) | A `web_search` tool backed by a registered search tool | `web_search` |
| [Speculation](/docs/boons/speculation) | A fast drafter answers when the model itself verifies the draft | `speculation` |
| [Knowledge](/docs/boons/knowledge) | Passages from your document collections, placed ahead of the conversation | `knowledge` |
| [Compression](/docs/boons/compression) | Long inputs made smaller before the model reads them | `compression` |

[Guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails) run on the same engine but are set per tenant, not per model.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: The `x-obleth-boons` header
chunks.text:
On a response, the header lists what acted on the request: `vision`, `knowledge`, `compression`, `tool_loop`, `image_generation`, `web_search`, `structured_output`, `guardrails_input`, `speculation`.

On a request, it takes comma-separated tokens:

- `off` turns every boon off for that request. The tenant's guardrails still run.
- `lossy` turns compression's lossy pass on for that request. See [Compression](/docs/boons/compression).

A helper call goes through the same endpoint selection as a normal request: a healthy endpoint of the helper model, with that endpoint's key. Models with no `api_base` of their own, such as those launched on Slurm, work as helpers. Helper replies are read with a size cap. Helper rows record zero energy, because the hardware time falls inside the main request.

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: Turn a boon on
chunks.text:
A boon runs only when it is on for the gateway **and** the model asks for it. Nothing is granted by default.

Open **Settings › Boons**. Each boon is a row with its switch, what it is set to, and the models asking for it. A row reads "1 asks, off" when a model has the boon but the switch is off. **Open** a row to pick its helper model and limits, then save with the save bar. The gateway picks up the change within 15 seconds, with no restart.

Knowledge is the exception: its row links to the Knowledge page, where retrieval is switched on.

Open the model's page and go to **Boons**. Switch the boon on and save. A boon that is off in Settings, or has no helper model picked, can't be newly granted; the page says what is missing.

The tool loop is granted by ticking MCP servers under the model's **Tool servers** instead. Attaching a knowledge collection to a model grants it Knowledge.

Send a request and read the `x-obleth-boons` response header, which lists the boons that acted on it. **Settings › Needs you** also lists any boon a model asks for while it is off, or is on with no helper model picked.

The same two switches from the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "vision_enabled": true, "vision_fallback_model": "glm-4-5v" }'

curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: appl

chunks.title: Boons
chunks.heading: What callers see
chunks.text: A model's entry on `GET /v1/models/{id}` and `/model/info` lists its boons in `boon_details`, next to its own `supports_*` flags: whether each boon runs, and which helper model does the work. A text-only model with Vision reports `supports_vision: false` and names its describer, so a result can be traced to both models. See [Model discovery](/docs/clients/openai-compatible-api#the-models-own-abilities-and-its-boons).

chunks.title: Speculation
chunks.heading: A request where it helps
chunks.text:
Nothing changes for the client:

```bash
curl http://localhost/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5-3",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python function that merges two sorted lists."}]
  }'
```

The response carries `x-obleth-boons: speculation` when the cascade was armed. The gateway logs whether the draft shipped, was deferred or escalated, and why.

chunks.title: Speculation
chunks.heading: How a draft is judged
chunks.text:
The scorer returns two numbers for a draft: **agreement**, the share of draft tokens the target would itself have picked first, and the **mean log-probability** of the draft tokens. A draft at or above both ship floors (**Ship when**) is released.

For a streaming client the draft is checked as it grows: first after **First check** tokens, then every **Every** tokens.

| Zone | Condition | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pass | agreement ≥ ship floor and log-probability ≥ ship floor | The verified span is sent |
| Give up | agreement or log-probability below the **Give up when** floors | Drafting stops; the target answers |
| Defer | anything between | Keep drafting and check again |

If nothing has been sent by **Decide by** tokens, the target answers. Once a span has been sent, a later failed check has the target continue the sent text rather than start over, so the client never sees its answer rewritten. Sent spans play back at **Streaming pace**, a third of it once the draft is complete. The next span is checked while the current one plays back, so a check pauses the stream only when it takes longer than a span's playback.

chunks.title: Speculation
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A fast drafter model, and a deployment of the target whose backend serves `prompt_logprobs`
  Settings › Boons › Speculation, then the model's page › Boons
  Draft and verify calls, billed as `speculation_draft` and `speculation_verify`

A fast drafter writes the answer, and a scoring deployment of the target checks every draft token in one `prompt_logprobs` prefill, far cheaper than the target writing those tokens. A draft that passes is sent; one that doesn't is dropped and the target answers. The client only ever gets text the target verified or wrote.

chunks.title: Speculation
chunks.heading: Profiles
chunks.text:
| Profile | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Calibrated** | Drafts only in categories where drafts verify reliably (coding, math, summarization, writing), each with its own ship floor, and sends infrastructure, planning, database, regex, explanation and debugging straight to the target before any draft is paid for. Needs a classifier. |
| **Cautious** | Drafts every eligible request and holds it to one strict gate (the defaults below). Works without a classifier. |
| **Custom** | Shown when you change any value by hand. |

chunks.title: Speculation
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Speculation on | `speculation_enabled` | `false` |
| Drafter | `speculation_draft_model` | none; the fleet default for targets without their own |
| Classifier | `speculation_classify_model` | none |
| Categories | `speculation_category_gates` | `[]`, as `[{tag, speculate, agree_min, lp_min}]` |
| Try a draft for categories not listed | `speculation_unlisted_categories_speculate` | `true` |
| Scoring endpoint | `speculation_verify_url_template` | empty |
| Agreement to ship | `speculation_agree_min` | `0.5` (0 to 1) |
| Confidence to ship | `speculation_lp_min` | `-1.0` (0 or below) |
| Agreement to give up | `speculation_abort_agree` | `0.45` |
| Confidence to give up | `speculation_abort_lp` | `-1.6` |
| First check | `speculation_first_chunk_tokens` | `80` tokens |
| Every | `speculation_chunk_tokens` | `250` tokens |
| Decide by | `speculation_decide_by_tokens` | `450` tokens |
| Longest draft | `speculation_max_draft_tokens` | `2048` tokens |
| Streaming pace | `speculation_pace_ms` | `9` ms; `0` sends each span at once |
| Budget | `speculation_timeout_ms` | `45000` ms before anything is sent |
| Drafter template arguments | `speculation_draft_chat_template_kwargs` | none; for example `{"reasoning": false}`, sent to the drafter only |

An omitted field keeps its stored value, and so does `0` for the token counts and the budget. An out-of-range floor is ignored. `""` clears the drafter, the classifier or the temp

chunks.title: Speculation
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
The target needs a deployment whose backend supports `prompt_logprobs` and serves `/tokenize` at the server root, at a direct URL rather than through another gateway. Backends that can't take `prompt_logprobs` scoring may fail under it.

Open **Settings › Boons**, switch **Speculation** on and **Open** its row. Choose a **Profile**, pick the fleet **Drafter** and, for the Calibrated profile, a **Classifier**. Under **Advanced**, set the **Scoring endpoint** URL template if your scoring deployments follow a naming rule. Save with the save bar.

On the target model's page, switch **Speculation** on under **Boons**. Its cascade settings appear: pick this model's own **Drafter**, or leave the fleet default. Under **Advanced wiring**, set **Scoring endpoint URL** if this model's scorer isn't covered by the fleet template, and **Scoring endpoint serves** if that backend uses a different model name. Save.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "speculation_enabled": true,
    "speculation_draft_model": "qwen3-4b",
    "speculation_verify_url_template": "http://{upstream}-scoring.serving.svc.cluster.local:8000/v1"
  }'

curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "boons": ["speculation"], "draft_model": "qwen3-4b" }'
```

chunks.title: Structured output
chunks.heading: Ask for JSON

chunks.title: Structured output
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Nothing extra; a separate fixer model is optional
  Settings › Boons › Structured output, then the model's page › Boons
  A repair call only when a reply fails, billed as `structured_output_boon`

chunks.title: Structured output
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structured output on | `structured_output_enabled` | `false` |
| Fixer model | `structured_output_fixer_model` | none: the request's own model |
| Retries | `structured_output_max_repair_attempts` | `1`, at most `3`; `0` turns repair off |
| Repair timeout | `structured_output_timeout_ms` | `30000` ms, per repair call |

The boon runs when Structured output is on in Settings, the model has `structured_output` in its `boons` list and is not flagged `supports_response_schema`, and the request is a chat completion whose `response_format.type` is `json_schema` or `json_object`.

If the fixer model is missing or disabled, the request's own model does the repair.

While the boon is active the gateway calls the model without streaming, checks the whole reply, and then sends it. A client that asked for `stream: true` still gets a stream, but it starts only once the reply is complete, so allow a longer client timeout. The gateway's own upstream timeout for these requests is at least 120 seconds.

Schemas larger than 64 KB are put in the prompt but not validated; the reply is only checked for valid JSON.

If every repair fails, the model's original reply passes through unchanged and the response carries `x-obleth-boons-warning: structured_output_validation_failed`.

With the [image generation](/docs/boons/image-generation) boon on the same request, the validated JSON wins: generated images are not attached, and the response car

chunks.title: Structured output
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Open **Settings › Boons**, switch **Structured output** on and **Open** its row. Under **Fixer**, pick the model that repairs broken replies, or leave "The same model, asked again". Set **Retries** (at most 3) and the **Repair timeout**. Save with the save bar.

On the model's page, go to **Boons**, switch **Structured output** on and save. Leave **Response schema** under **Native** off: a model that supports `response_format` itself doesn't need the boon, and the boon steps aside for it.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "structured_output_enabled": true,
    "structured_output_fixer_model": "qwen3-235b",
    "structured_output_max_repair_attempts": 1,
    "structured_output_timeout_ms": 30000
  }'
```

Send `structured_output_fixer_model` as `""` to repair with the request's own model.

chunks.title: Structured output
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
The gateway removes `response_format` from the request and adds a system message after any existing ones:

```text
# Response format

Respond with a single JSON document that conforms to the JSON Schema below. Output only the JSON document — no prose, no markdown fences, nothing before or after it.

JSON Schema: {"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":["birth_year","name"]}
```

A model flagged as not supporting system messages gets the section at the start of the first user message instead.

When the model replies, the gateway finds the JSON document in the text (tolerating fences and stray prose) and validates it. A valid document replaces the reply's content. An invalid one goes to the fixer with the validation errors, up to **Retries** times.

chunks.title: Tool loop
chunks.heading: Ask something that needs a tool
chunks.text:
With a web-search server granted, a plain question is enough:

```bash
curl http://localhost/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5-3",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the latest vLLM release?"}]
  }'
```

The response carries `x-obleth-boons: tool_loop` and contains the final answer only, never `tool_calls`. The final answer streams token by token. While tools run between turns, the stream sends a one-line marker naming each tool call on the reasoning channel (`reasoning_content`), not in the answer.

chunks.title: Tool loop
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A registered MCP server and a model with function calling
  Settings › Boons › Tool loop, then the model's page › Tool servers
  Each follow-up model turn, billed as `tool_loop`

The client sends an ordinary chat request with no tools. The gateway adds the granted servers' tools, runs each tool call the model makes against its MCP server, appends the result, and asks the model again until it answers. Registering servers and calling them directly are covered in [MCP gateway](/docs/clients/mcp-gateway).

chunks.title: Tool loop
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool loop on | `tool_loop_enabled` | `false` |
| Turns | `tool_loop_max_turns` | `4`, at most `8` |
| Tool timeout | `tool_loop_tool_timeout_ms` | `30000` ms, per tool call |
| Request deadline | `tool_loop_deadline_secs` | `300` s for the whole loop, `1` to `3600` |
| Tool nudge | `tool_loop_nudge` | built-in text; `""` puts the default back |

A `0` for any number keeps the stored value.

The loop runs on a chat request when the Tool loop is on in Settings, the model has at least one server in its `tool_servers` list, and the model is flagged `supports_function_calling`. A model granted servers without function calling gets no tools, and the gateway logs a warning.

Deleting an MCP server removes it from every model's `tool_servers`.

- **Turns.** When the model is still asking for tools after the last turn, the gateway removes the tools and asks it to answer from what it has gathered.
- **Calls per turn.** At most 16 tool calls run from one model reply; each call past that gets an error result instead. The calls of one reply run at the same time, up to 8 at once and 4 at once against one MCP server, and their results go back to the model in the order it made them. Web-search and image limits are shared out among them in that order, so a call past a limit is refused as it would be if the calls ran one after another.
- **Request deadline.** Once it passes, the loop dispatches nothing more. Without streaming, it retur

chunks.title: Tool loop
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Add the server on the **MCP Servers** page. The page checks each server when it opens and lists its tools, so you can see it answers before granting it.

Open **Settings › Boons**, switch **Tool loop** on and **Open** its row. Set **Turns**, **Tool timeout** and **Request deadline** under **Limits**, and edit the **Tool nudge** if you need to. Save with the save bar.

On the model's page, turn on **Function calling** and **Tool choice** under **Native**; the dashboard lets you grant tools only when both are on. Then tick the server under **Tool servers** and save. You can also grant it from the server's panel on the MCP Servers page.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "tool_loop_enabled": true,
    "tool_loop_max_turns": 4,
    "tool_loop_tool_timeout_ms": 30000,
    "tool_loop_deadline_secs": 300
  }'

curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "upstream_model": "Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    "api_base": "http://inference.example.internal:8000/v1",
    "supports_function_calling": true,
    "tool_servers": ["searxng"]
  }'
```

chunks.title: Tool loop
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
- The granted servers' tools, merged into the request's `tools`.
- For a client that sent no tools of its own, the **Tool nudge** as a system message: it tells the model it has tools and to use them for current or external facts rather than guessing.
- After each tool call, the result as a `tool` message, cut to 16,000 characters.

A client that brings its own `tools`, such as an IDE assistant, keeps them. The granted tools are added alongside, the gateway runs only its own, and any call to the client's tools goes back to the client unchanged. No nudge is added for such clients.

chunks.title: Vision
chunks.heading: Descriptions are reused
chunks.text:
A conversation sends its earlier images again on every turn. Each description is kept for **Keep descriptions** (6 hours by default) and used again when the same tenant sends the same image to the same describer with the same prompt, so an image is described once per conversation rather than once per turn. An image repeated within one request is also described once. A reused description makes no describer call and is not billed. Changing the describer or the prompt describes images again.

Descriptions are kept in the gateway's Redis, per tenant: one tenant's description is never given to another. Set **Keep descriptions** to `0` to turn reuse off.

chunks.title: Vision
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A registered chat model that can see images, to act as the describer
  Settings › Boons › Vision, then the model's page › Boons
  One describer call per image, billed as `vision_boon`; an image sent again in the same conversation is not described again

chunks.title: Vision
chunks.heading: Send an image

chunks.title: Vision
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vision on | `vision_enabled` | `false` |
| Describer model | `vision_fallback_model` | none; `""` clears it, which turns the boon off |
| Images per request | `vision_max_images` | `6` |
| Describe timeout | `vision_timeout_ms` | `30000` ms, per image |
| Keep descriptions | `vision_cache_ttl_secs` | `21600` s (6 hours); `0` turns reuse off |
| Describe prompt | `vision_describe_prompt` | built-in prompt asking for what is clearly visible |

A `0` for **Images per request** or **Describe timeout** keeps the stored value. A saved prompt still equal to the earlier built-in one follows the current built-in prompt.

The boon runs on a chat request only when all of these hold:

- Vision is on in Settings and a describer model is picked.
- The model has `vision` in its `boons` list.
- The model is not flagged `supports_vision`. A model that sees images natively gets its images unchanged, even if it holds the boon.
- The request contains at least one `image_url` content part.

A registered vision model is one option and the boon is the other: give a model that sees images the `vision` tag instead of the boon. For image, audio and embedding endpoints as first-class models, see [Images, audio and speech](/docs/clients/multi-modal-models).

Images are described concurrently, so the added latency is about one describer call, not one per image, and none for images described earlier in the conversation. Only the first **Images per

chunks.title: Vision
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
On the describer model's page, add the `vision` tag under **Routing** and save. The tag sets the model's `supports_vision` flag, which makes it selectable as a describer. Through the Management API, send `"supports_vision": true` on the model.

Open **Settings › Boons**, switch **Vision** on and **Open** its row. Pick the **Describer model**, and adjust **Images per request**, **Describe timeout**, **Keep descriptions** and the **Describe prompt** if you need to. Save with the save bar.

On the text-only model's page, go to **Boons**, switch **Vision** on and save.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "vision_enabled": true,
    "vision_fallback_model": "glm-4-5v",
    "vision_max_images": 6,
    "vision_timeout_ms": 30000
  }'

curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models/$MODEL_ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "boons": ["vision"] }'
```

chunks.title: Vision
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
Each image part is replaced, in place, by a text part:

```text
[Image description: A dialog titled "Disk full" with the text "Cannot save report.pdf: 0 bytes free on /home" and two buttons, Retry and Cancel.]
```

The model never receives the image. It answers from the description. By default the describer is asked for the main subjects and what they are doing, the setting, all readable text verbatim, and any UI elements, code, diagrams, charts or layout, and to say when text is too small or blurry to read rather than guess.

The describer gets the image before the prompt, at temperature 0 and with at most 700 output tokens, so the same image gets the same description.

chunks.title: Web search
chunks.heading: Ask something current
chunks.text:
```bash
curl http://localhost/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "my-chat-model",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What changed in the latest PostgreSQL minor release?"}]
  }'
```

The model calls `web_search`, the gateway runs the search and hands back the results, and the model answers citing the URLs it used. The response carries `x-obleth-boons: web_search` and holds the final answer only, never the tool call.

On a streaming request, each search shows as a one-line marker on the reasoning channel (`reasoning_content`) naming the tool and the query, so a client sees the work while the stream waits for the results.

chunks.title: Web search
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A registered search tool and a chat model with function calling
  Settings › Boons › Web search, then the model's page › Boons
  Nothing per search; the model's follow-up turns bill as `tool_loop`

chunks.title: Web search
chunks.heading: Settings
chunks.text:
| Settings label | Field | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web search on | `web_search_enabled` | `false` |
| Search tool | `web_search_tool` | none; must be a `search` model. `""` clears it, which turns the boon off |
| Results per search | `web_search_max_results` | `5`, at most `10` |
| Searches per request | `web_search_max_searches_per_request` | `3`, at most `8` |
| Search timeout | `web_search_timeout_ms` | `15000` ms, per search |
| Tool description | `web_search_tool_description` | built-in text; `""` puts the default back |

A `0` for any number keeps the stored value.

The tool is added when Web search is on in Settings with a search tool picked, the model has `web_search` in its `boons` list, and the model is flagged `supports_function_calling`. Without function calling the model gets no tool and the gateway logs a warning; the model's page marks the boon as doing nothing, and **Settings › Needs you** lists the model.

If the client already defines a tool named `web_search`, or a granted MCP server exposes one, that tool wins and the boon is inactive for the request.

A model can hold this boon with [image generation](/docs/boons/image-generation) and [speculation](/docs/boons/speculation). When the speculation classifier can't place a request in a category, speculation abstains so the model can search.

- Searches run inside the gateway's tool loop, so the [Tool loop](/docs/boons/tool-loop)'s **Turns** and **Request deadline** apply, even with its switch off. A s

chunks.title: Web search
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Add a model of type **Web search (SearXNG)** (`search`) whose API base is a SearXNG instance with JSON output on. See [Register a search tool](/docs/clients/search-api#register-a-search-tool).

Open **Settings › Boons**, switch **Web search** on and **Open** its row. Pick the **Search tool**, then set **Results per search**, **Searches per request** and **Search timeout** under **Limits**. Save with the save bar. Until a search tool is picked, **Settings › Needs you** says so.

On the chat model's page, turn on **Function calling** under **Native**, then switch **Web search** on under **Boons** and save. The model calls the tool itself, so the switch can't be turned on while Function calling is off, and turning Function calling off turns it off.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:9180/api/v1/settings/boons \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "web_search_enabled": true,
    "web_search_tool": "web",
    "web_search_max_results": 5,
    "web_search_max_searches_per_request": 3,
    "web_search_timeout_ms": 15000
  }'
```

Then add `web_search` to the model's `boons`, with `supports_function_calling: true`. The Tool loop switch doesn't need to be on; web search works without it.

chunks.title: Web search
chunks.heading: What the model sees
chunks.text:
- A `web_search` tool with `query`, a short search-engine query, and optional `domains`, a list of sites to keep results to (at most 10). It is described by the **Tool description**, which says when to search and when to answer directly, followed by today's date (UTC) and a reminder to put the year or date in queries about anything recent.
- For a client that sent no tools and has no tool-loop nudge, a short system note: the tool exists, call it for current or external facts and cite the URLs, and don't offer searching otherwise.
- After each search, a numbered list of results: title, URL, publication date when known, and a snippet cut to 400 characters, ending with a request to cite the URLs it relies on. While the request has searches left, the list also says to search again with different keywords when the results don't answer the question.
- When nothing was found, a sentence saying so: the model can search again with different keywords while it has searches left, or answer from what it knows.
- When the search could not run, a sentence saying so and telling the model to answer from what it knows. The request never fails because of the boon.

chunks.title: Worker agents
chunks.heading: Ask for agents
chunks.text:
Ask for the work in any chat: "explore this codebase with four agents and tell me how auth works", or "use sub-agents to compare these three approaches". The model splits the work into tasks and sends each to a worker with its `delegate` tool. The workers run at the same time on a smaller, faster model, and their reports come back to the model, which does the deciding and writing.

A slow, strong model plus several fast workers finishes sooner, and the main model's context stays small because it reads reports instead of every file.

Workers run inside Chat. They never use your connections or clusters, so asking for agents never starts Slurm or Kubernetes jobs.

chunks.title: Worker agents
chunks.heading: Follow the work
chunks.text:
The reply shows one step for the workers, with each worker's title, what it's doing now, its steps and tokens. Open a finished worker to read its report. A worker that fails says why, and the model works with the reports that came back.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Workers per call | 6 |
| Steps per worker | 30 |
| Time per worker | 5 minutes |
| Output per worker step | 8,192 tokens |
| Workers running at once on one Chat replica | 24 |

Each worker is charged to you on its own usage record, under the worker model, so your daily allowance and usage by model include it. Workers use low thinking effort.

Administrators choose which models can be workers; see [Models, groups and limits](/docs/run-chat/models-and-limits#worker-models).

chunks.title: Worker agents
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
6 workers at once
  Read files, never change them
  Chosen by administrators
  A model with tool calling

chunks.title: Worker agents
chunks.heading: What workers can read
chunks.text:
A worker is a short chat of its own. It gets only its task, not your conversation, so the model writes each task to stand on its own.

- **In a chat with a workspace**, workers list, read and search its files and read its git history.
- **When the task needs a repository or the project's code** and the chat has no workspace yet, Chat turns the chat's workspace on first. Given a repository address, it clones the repository into `repos/` and tells each worker where it is. From your next message the model can use the workspace itself too.
- **Otherwise**, workers answer from what their model knows.

Workers can't change files, run commands or send work on to other workers.

chunks.title: Apps
chunks.heading: Call it from a program
chunks.text:
The **API** card shows the address and a `curl` example. Make a key there with **Create key**; it shows once.

```bash
curl https://chat.example.edu/api/apps/k7f3q2xm/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question": "Which samples failed?"}'
```

The body is the app's inputs as a JSON object. The answer is `{"runId", "status", "output", "error"}`: 200 when the run completed, 500 when it failed. A call runs the published version as the person who made the key, who must still be an administrator. An app has up to 10 keys; **Revoke** stops one at once.

chunks.title: Apps
chunks.heading: Chat with it
chunks.text:
A published app also answers at its chat page, `/a/<code>/<name>`; the **Chat page** card has the link. Sign-in leads back to the page.

- Each message runs the published version as the person chatting, with their own access to models and documents.
- The message goes into the app's first text input. Give the app a JSON input named `history` and it gets the earlier turns as `[{"role": "user" | "assistant", "content": "…"}]`.
- The reply is the app's output: text as it is, or an object's `answer`, `reply` or `text` field, otherwise the JSON.
- An app with other required inputs can't be used from a chat; the card and the page say which.
- The conversation stays in that browser tab. **New chat** starts over.

chunks.title: Apps
chunks.heading: Inputs and steps
chunks.text:
Inputs have a name, a type (text, number, true or false, or JSON) and can be required. Steps read the run through references: `{{inputs.question}}`, `{{steps.search}}` for an earlier step's result, and `{{item}}` and `{{index}}` inside **For each**. A value that is only a reference takes the value itself; anything else gets it as text.

| Step | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Agent | Asks a model, with optional instructions; can read the reply as JSON |
| Search knowledge | Searches the project's collections, or the ones you pick |
| Code | Runs JavaScript inside Chat, with 64 MB of memory, 5 seconds and no network or files |
| Decide | The model picks one of several described paths, each with its own steps |
| If | The first path whose rules all hold runs: empty, not empty, equals, contains, more than, less than, or one line of JavaScript |
| For each | Runs its steps once per item, up to 100 items, 4 at a time by default and at most 8 |
| HTTP request | Calls a public address, up to 30 seconds and 1 MB |
| Response | Ends the run with a value |

A path that ends in **Response** ends the app; otherwise the run carries on after **Decide** or **If**. An app has up to 60 steps, nested four deep. A run stops after five minutes.

chunks.title: Apps
chunks.heading: Make an app
chunks.text:
On **Projects**, choose **New app**, or open a project and choose **Make it an app**. In a chat, describe something people or programs will use, such as a chatbot over your documents, and the model offers an app with its first steps; **Create app** puts it in the chat's project.
  
  
    The **App** tab shows the steps on a canvas. Click a step type in the palette to add it after the selected step, or drag it onto a **+**. Select a step to edit it; the **Inputs** card sets what a call sends.
  
  
    **Try** runs the draft with the inputs you give and shows each step's result.
  
  
    **Publish** makes the draft the version that answers calls and the chat page. Later edits stay in the draft until you publish again; **Unpublish** turns both off.
  

Each app has an eight-character code that never changes, so renaming an app never breaks a caller. **Edit everything as JSON** shows the whole app as one document.

chunks.title: Apps
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A project you own, as an administrator
  The project's App tab
  An API with a key, or its chat page
  Chat itself, no workspace

For now only administrators make, call and chat with apps.

chunks.title: Apps
chunks.heading: Runs
chunks.text: **Recent runs** lists tests, API calls and chat messages for 7 days, each with its inputs, output and step-by-step trace.

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Cancel and delete
chunks.text:
**Cancel** stops the rows that haven't started; the rows that finished stay in the results.

**Delete** removes a batch for good: its answers on the gateway and the spreadsheet Chat kept to rebuild your results. Download the results first if you still need them. A running batch can't be deleted; cancel it first. Without a delete, batches are removed about a month after they were created.

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Download the results
chunks.text:
**Download results** gives back your spreadsheet with three columns added:

| Column | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` | The model's answer for that row |
| `status` | `done`, `failed`, `ran out of time`, `cancelled`, `skipped (blank)`, or while it runs, `waiting` |
| `error` | Why a row failed |

It works while the batch is still running, as **Results so far**, with the rows still to come marked `waiting`. The file starts with a byte order mark so Excel reads accents and symbols, and a cell that starts with `=`, `+` or `@`, or with a `-` that a spreadsheet would read as a formula, is written as text so a spreadsheet program doesn't run it. List items (`- first`) and negative numbers are left as they are.

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Keep them sorted
chunks.text:
- **Rename and tag:** a batch's **⋯** menu has **Rename and tag**. Tags are single words such as `#survey` or `#spring-2026`, up to 12 a batch. Only you see the names and tags you give.
- **Filter:** show all your batches, or only those running, done, needing a look (failed rows, out of time, couldn't start) or cancelled; click a tag to show only its batches; or search by name, model, file or `#tag`.
- **Select several:** tick batches, or tick the box above the list for every batch shown, then **Add tags** or **Delete**.

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Limits
chunks.text:
- Up to 50,000 rows and 200 columns per file, and 90 MB.
- Up to 10 batches running at once per person.
- Each request is tried up to 5 times when the model is busy or fails briefly.
- A batch runs at background priority: it never slows down people chatting, and a busy model runs it slowly.

Administrators: the page appears when Chat's gateway runs batches. See [Features and what they need](/docs/run-chat/features).

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Batches in the sidebar
  CSV or TSV, up to 50,000 rows
  The same spreadsheet with answer, status and error columns
  Only you

A batch sends one request per row of a spreadsheet: classify 5,000 survey answers, summarize every abstract in a reading list, pull fields out of a column of notes. The gateway runs it as a [batch](/docs/clients/batches), in the background, while models have room to spare, so it can take minutes or hours. You can close the page; it keeps going.

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Start a batch
chunks.text:
Open **Batches** and choose **New batch**, then choose or drop a CSV or TSV file. The first row names the columns; turn off **First row is column names** if yours has none, and the columns become `column_1`, `column_2` and so on. Save an Excel or Numbers file as CSV first.

New to it? **Try the example** loads a ten-row spreadsheet of product feedback with the prompt already written, and **Download it** saves the same file so you can see the format.

Write what each row should be sent as, and click a column's chip to put `{column}` into the prompt where the cursor is. Each row gets the prompt with its own values filled in:

```
Summarize this abstract in two sentences for a general reader.

Title: {title}
{abstract}
```

**Add instructions for every row** sends a system prompt before each one: the role, the format to answer in, what to leave out. "Answer with one word: positive, negative or mixed."

Choose the model (any chat model, but not **Auto**) and when it must finish: within a day, 3 days or a week. Rows that haven't run by then don't run. Give the batch a name if you like; it starts as the file's name.

The panel shows what the first rows will send. **Start batch** says how many requests it makes; blank rows are skipped.

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Watch it run
chunks.text:
Each batch shows a progress bar and what it is doing:

| Shown | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Running** | With the time left at the pace so far |
| **Waiting for the model** | People chatting have the model busy, and batches wait their turn. Nothing has finished for two minutes or more |
| **Done** | Every row ran; it says how many failed, if any |
| **Ran out of time** | The deadline passed with rows still waiting. The rows that ran are in the results |
| **Stopping**, **Cancelled** | You cancelled it. Rows already running finish first |
| **Couldn't start** | The requests had errors, with the first one shown |

The page updates on its own every few seconds while anything runs.

chunks.title: Browser
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A Chrome in a Kubernetes pod, with your sign-ins
  A tab, shown live in the side pane
  Form submissions, buying, sending, deleting
  A model with tool calling

chunks.title: Browser
chunks.heading: Take over
chunks.text:
Press **Take over** to drive the tab yourself: your clicks, scrolling, typing and pasting go to the page, and the address bar opens any address. The model is paused while you have control. It gets nothing from the tab, no page text and none of your typing, and its browser tools refuse to run.

The model hands you the tab itself when a page needs you: a sign-in, a password, a captcha or bot check, a payment or a choice only you can make. Its reply ends with **Your turn in the browser** and what to do. When you're done, **Hand back** returns the tab and the chat carries on.

The model never types passwords. Sites you sign in to keep you signed in, so it can read pages behind your sign-in, such as a journal your library pays for.

chunks.title: Browser
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Press **Browser** in the composer. If you ask for something that needs a real page in a chat without it, the model asks first: its reply ends with **Turn on browser**, which turns it on and carries on with your request.

Ask for something to look up: "what changed in the latest vLLM release?" The model finds pages, opens the promising ones and reads them before it answers, and says which pages it used. When your installation gives models web search (an Obleth gateway with search on), the model searches with that, which is faster, and uses the browser to read and use the pages. Without it, or when a search finds nothing useful, it searches in the browser. The tab appears in the **Browser** tab of the side pane, live, so you can watch it work. In a chat with a workspace, Browser sits next to Preview, Files and Terminal.

Each step of the reply shows what the model did (searched, opened, clicked, typed) with a small picture of the page at that moment. They group under **Browse** in the reply's work.

chunks.title: Browser
chunks.heading: What asks first
chunks.text:
Reading, scrolling, searching and following links never ask. Before the model submits a form, or presses a button that buys, sends, posts, publishes or deletes something, the step waits with the question, such as "Press “Submit order” on shop.example?":

- **Allow once** runs this step.
- **Always on this site** runs it and doesn't ask again for that site.
- **Deny** skips it, and the model is told not to try another way.

A chat in [Auto mode](/docs/chat/connections#auto-mode) doesn't ask.

Text on web pages is information for the model, never instructions: it's told to ignore anything on a page that asks it to do something you didn't ask for.

chunks.title: Browser
chunks.heading: Your browser
chunks.text:
**Settings › Personal › Browser** shows whether your browser is running and its tabs, one per chat. There you can:

- **Search with** DuckDuckGo, Google or Bing, for the searches the model runs in your browser.
- Remove sites you allowed with **Always on this site**.
- **Sleep now** stops the browser. Your sign-ins are kept.
- **Forget all browser data** deletes sign-ins, cookies and history, closes every chat's tab and removes the sites you allowed.

Your browser sleeps after 15 minutes unused and starts again, in a few seconds, when the model browses or you press **Open the browser**. Watching the tab keeps it awake. Its data is deleted 7 days after you last used it.

Downloads aren't kept yet: a link to a file such as a PDF doesn't open. The model gives you the link instead.

Your browser is a headless Chromium in its own pod, beside your workspace, under the same rules: it reaches only public web addresses (not Chat's network, the cluster or your LAN), and only Chat can connect to it. Each person's browser and sign-ins are separate. The live view accepts connections only from Chat's own origin, and only the chat's owner can watch or drive the tab.

Each page comes back as text: headings, paragraphs, list items and table rows, with every link, button and field numbered, such as `[12] link "Release notes" → github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases`. The model clicks and types by number. Long pages come in windows of about 7,000 characters, which it reads on with `browser_read`

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.heading: Add a connection
chunks.text:
You can add your own connections, and administrators can share one with every account. Every active connection is on in a new chat; the composer's **Tools** button and the chat's **Details** tab switch them per chat. You can switch a shared connection off for all your chats.

  
    MCP server
    Slurm
    Kubernetes
  
  

In **Settings › MCP servers**, add the server's URL and, if it needs one, an access token (sent as `Authorization: Bearer`). Chat connects once to list the tools and keeps that list until you edit or refresh the connection.

Chat speaks the Streamable HTTP transport (protocol `2025-06-18`). Servers that only offer the older SSE transport, or that need an OAuth sign-in, aren't supported yet.

  
  

In **Compute › Clusters**, add the slurmrestd URL, your Slurm user name and a JWT from `scontrol token`. slurmrestd must run with `rest_auth/jwt`. Chat finds the newest REST API version it offers, from v0.0.40 to v0.0.45; for a newer one, enter it in **REST API version**.

```bash
scontrol token username=$USER lifespan=2592000
# Paste the part after SLURM_JWT=
```

Tools: what the cluster's partitions can run now (idle nodes, CPUs and GPUs, with one partition's nodes when asked), your jobs (or everyone's when asked), including the ones that ended in the last days with their exit codes, a job's details, submit and cancel.

  
  

In **Compute › Clusters**, add the API server URL, your bearer token, the namespace and, for a private CA, its certificate. The cluste

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.heading: Approve what the model does
chunks.text:
Tools that only read run without asking: MCP tools marked `readOnlyHint`, and the Slurm and Kubernetes tools that list, get or read logs. Any other tool waits on a card in the answer with **Allow** and **Deny**, for up to 15 minutes.

![A Kubernetes apply waiting for approval: Allow, Allow for this chat and Deny, above the Deployment manifest the model wants to apply](/chat/approval.png)

The card shows what Chat read from the call: for a Kubernetes or Slurm change, the resources or script it will act on, worked out by the server the same way the call is carried out, with every argument in full beneath. A call whose arguments are too long to show whole (384 KB) is refused. Each card covers one call: an approval is used up when it is read, and a later call never runs on an earlier one's answer.

**Allow for this chat** lets that one tool run without asking for the rest of the conversation. A connection can also be set never to ask. Decisions are stored in Postgres, so the answer continues on whichever replica picks it up.

![A chat asking how busy a Slurm cluster is: the model read its partitions, node and queue with read-only tools, without asking](/chat/cluster-chat.png)

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.heading: Auto mode
chunks.text:
In **Tools** in the composer, switch on **Auto mode** to let every tool in that chat run without asking, including ones that submit, apply or delete. The **Tools** button then shows **Auto**. Use it for long work you won't be watching, such as research runs, which start in Auto mode. A turn in Auto mode also keeps going after your sign-in ends; see [Long turns](/docs/chat/workspaces#long-turns). Tools still act with your own tokens, so they can do only what you can. Your administrator can turn Auto mode off for the installation.

- Each tool appears to the model as `<connection name>__<tool>`, up to 128 tools per request.
- For models whose tool calls Chat reads from the reply's text, a call the model only shows, inside a code block, a code span or a quoted line, is left as text and not run.
- Kubernetes tools take a namespace, a name and an API version, each checked to be a name of its kind, and every request goes to the cluster address the connection was saved with. `get` on a Secret shows its keys and the size of each, as `kubectl describe` does, never the values.
- People who don't manage a shared connection see its address without the path or query, which often carry an MCP server's key.
- Tool output is cut to 48 KiB for the model. A call times out after 2 minutes.
- Your own connections must use `https` and reach public addresses. Chat resolves the host itself, refuses loopback, private and link-local ranges, and follows no redirects. Shared connections, and an adminis

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Settings › MCP servers
  Compute › Clusters
  Compute › Devices
  Your own token
  Ask first, by default

chunks.title: Connections
chunks.heading: See a cluster live
chunks.text:
**Compute › Clusters** shows each cluster as your account sees it, refreshed every 30 seconds:

- **Slurm**: CPUs, GPUs and memory in use, how many nodes are idle or unavailable, the queue, your running and pending jobs, your jobs that ended in the last 7 days with their exit codes, and each partition's idle nodes, CPUs and GPUs with its time limit. Idle means free to start a job now: nodes that are down, drained or in maintenance never count. Chat lists a cluster's nodes at most once every 30 seconds and shares that with everyone looking, while partitions and your jobs are always asked with your own token.

On a Slurm cluster set to bring job output back, the model can also read what a job it submitted printed, once the job ends, with **Job output**: the last 1 MiB of its output file. **Job details** works for finished jobs too, from the cluster's accounting.
- **Kubernetes**: quota use, pods, deployments, jobs, nodes when you may list them, and what you may do in the namespace.

![Compute › Clusters showing a Slurm cluster as the demo account: CPUs and memory in use, nodes, the queue, partitions and nodes](/chat/clusters.png)

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Chat details
chunks.text:
Under the chat's title, the project pill moves the chat into a project or starts a project from it, and the knowledge pill picks the collections it searches.

Everything else about the chat is in the **Details** tab of the side pane: how much context it uses (messages, and the tools, instructions and pages sent with them, as of the last request the latest reply sent), the model and parameters with **Adjust**, its project, knowledge and tools. Open it from **Details** in the top bar, the hover card on the send button, the project pill's menu, or ⌘ .. It opens beside the chat, next to the workspace's and browser's tabs, so it never covers what you're reading.

A reply streams in as it's written. When the model thinks out loud, its thinking goes in a collapsible panel above the answer. Thinking is saved, but only the answer is sent back to the model on later turns. A reply that ran out of tokens while thinking says so and suggests a higher output limit or a lower effort.

When a reply hasn't started after 3 seconds because its model is full, it says so, with how many requests are running and waiting, and your message stays in line. If you have reached your own limit of requests at once on that model, it says that instead. It also offers one of your favorite models, or your default, that isn't full, or **Auto**: switching stops the waiting reply and sends your message again with that model. If the gateway stops waiting for a slot, the reply says the model stayed full and offers t

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Edit, retry and branch
chunks.text:
- **Edit** a message and send it again, or **Regenerate** a reply. Both create a new version in the same chat. The previous and next arrows step through versions and bring back the turns that followed each one.
- **Branch** copies the chat up to a message into a new conversation.
- **Generation details** under a reply shows the model that answered, the parameters it used, token counts, how fast it wrote (output tokens per second of writing) and how long the first token took, the finish reason and, for a failure, why it failed. When the gateway measures energy, it also shows the energy the reply used and its CO₂.

Replies can draw math, diagrams, charts, molecules and tables; see [What Chat draws](/docs/chat/formatting).

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Find past chats
chunks.text: **All chats** searches titles and message text, and lists pinned chats first. Select several to archive, delete or export them together. **Export** writes portable JSON with the selected transcript and the bytes of its files, leaving out and naming any file too large to fit; **Import** brings it back as new private chats. One Chat export holds up to 50 conversations and 10 MiB.

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Import from other apps
chunks.text:
**All chats › Import** also takes your history from other chat apps. Chat works out which app a file came from.

| From | Export it with | Choose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open WebUI | Settings › Data Controls › Export Chats | The `.json` file |
| ChatGPT | Settings › Data controls › Export data | The `.zip` it emails, or the `conversations.json` inside it |
| Claude | Settings › Privacy › Export data | The `.zip`, or the `conversations.json` inside it |

- **Up to 200 MB and 5,000 conversations per file.** A ChatGPT zip full of images can be larger; unzip it and choose `conversations.json`. Chat keeps at most 256 MiB of text from one file and 64 MiB from one conversation; a file with a conversation over that is refused with a message saying which. An upload that stops arriving is dropped after 30 seconds.
- **What comes over.** Each chat shows the path its app was showing, with titles and dates, and pinned and archived chats stay that way where the app records it. Edited messages and regenerated replies become versions you step through with the arrows. Each reply keeps the name of the model that wrote it, and you continue the chat with your own default model.
- **What doesn't.** Images and files become a line such as `[Image not imported]`. System prompts and the app's hidden or tool steps are left out. Open WebUI folders and tags aren't carried over.
- **Again is safe.** Importing the same file again adds only the chats that aren't here yet.
- **Limits still apply.** A chat k

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Your Postgres, private to you
  After you close the tab
  Portable JSON, with files

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Rate a reply
chunks.text:
Thumbs up and thumbs down sit under each finished reply in your own chats. Thumbs down opens an optional form: pick reasons (wrong or made up, didn't follow instructions, too long, too short, harmful or offensive, other) and add a comment of up to 2,000 characters. Click the thumb you chose again to clear it, or the other one to change it.

Ratings stay in Chat and go to your administrators as counts per model, with the reasons and comments. They don't see which chat or reply a rating came from, or who gave it. People reading a chat you shared don't see your ratings.

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Send a message
chunks.text:
Type in the composer and press Enter. Under the box, **+** attaches files or adds Knowledge collections, and the dock switches the workspace, the browser and tools on for this chat; the ones that are on light up and show their names. The model pill on the right picks the model and the thinking effort, and the ring around the send button shows how much of the model's context the chat uses.

- **Model.** The picker lists the models your administrator published for you. The model you pick becomes your default for new chats. **Auto** sends `model: "auto"`, and the gateway picks a model for each message from its Auto-eligible models, filtered by what the message needs (tools, images, context length). The model that answered is shown on the reply. See [Auto routing](/docs/routing/auto-model-routing).
- **How busy a model is.** When the gateway reports load ([obleth](/docs/clients/model-load) does), a model's icon in the picker and on the model pill turns amber while it is busy, red while it is full, and faint while it has no servers running. A free model looks as usual. Hover for how many requests are running on how many slots.
- **Thinking effort.** Set in the model pill's popup and shown as bars on the pill: None, Low, Medium or High, passed to the model as `reasoning_effort`. With Auto, None and Low also steer the router toward a lighter model, and High toward a stronger one. Models that don't support a level may ignore it.
- **Parameters.** Temperature, the output limit and ins

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Send feedback
chunks.text: To report a problem or suggest something you'd like to see, choose **Feedback** in the sidebar. Pick what kind it is, write it, and choose **Send**. It goes to the people who run your site with the page you were on. They see your name only if you tick **You can contact me about this**.

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Share a chat
chunks.text:
The link button in a chat's header, or **Share…** in its options menu, shares it read-only:

- **Only you**: nobody else can open it.
- **A group**: members find it on the group's page.
- **Anyone signed in with the link**: every account here can open it from **Copy link**.

The link is the chat's own address. People you share with read it as it grows and open its files and images. They see the model, its settings and each tool step with what it returned, but not your instructions or what Chat recalled or learned about you while answering. **Fork to continue** copies it into a chat of their own, with its own copies of the files, the generated images its replies show, and the model and its settings, but not your instructions or memories. Everything that changes the chat stays yours, and its workspace, browser and connections are never shared. Choosing **Only you**, or deleting the group, ends access at once.

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Temporary chats
chunks.text:
Turn on **Temporary chat** beside the model picker before you send the first message. A temporary chat isn't kept:

- It stays out of your recent chats, **All chats** and search.
- It can't be shared, exported, branched, moved into a project or saved to your Library.
- It's deleted when you leave it: when you open another chat or page, start a new chat, sign out, close the tab or reload the page. A reply still running then is stopped. Chat also deletes any temporary chat that has been quiet for 23 hours.

While you're in one, the chat is marked **Temporary** and a note says it's deleted when you leave. A new chat started inside a project can't be temporary.

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: While it answers
chunks.text:
Responses run on the server. Close the tab, reload or switch chats, and the response keeps going; open the chat again and it picks up where it is. **Stop** ends only the response you see, never a newer one. You can run one response per chat and three at once by default.

When an answer finishes, Chat may offer three follow-up prompts under it. Click one to send it.

A model with tools can also ask you questions with `ask_user`. The reply ends with a card of one to four questions, each with a few options, one sometimes marked recommended. Step through them, pick options or write your own, and **Submit answers** sends them as your next message. Typing a message instead answers in your own words.

![A reply that ends with a question card: where the weekly benchmark should run, with Campus HPC (Slurm) recommended, Lab cluster (K8s), Both, or your own answer](/chat/questions.png)

chunks.title: Conversations
chunks.heading: Your usage
chunks.text: **Settings › Personal** opens with your last 30 days: requests and tokens, a chart of input and output tokens per day, which models they went to, and how much of today's allowance is left. Hover a day for its numbers, or open **Show as a table**. Days run in UTC, and allowances reset at 00:00 UTC.

chunks.title: Devices
chunks.heading: Add a device
chunks.text:
