chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Storage
chunks.text:
Batches keep their bytes in the gateway's object store, one S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Ceph, PowerScale, SeaweedFS, R2 and the like), never in Postgres. Postgres holds only state: a batch's status and counts, and per request its place in the input file, its status, attempts and the size of its answer.

Turning the object store on is one setting with a bucket and a key; batches are on whenever it is.

| Setting | Helm | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (Helm only) | `obleth.objectStorage.enabled` | `true` sets the variables below. Off, `/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` are not served and no runner starts |
| `OBLETH_S3_BUCKET` | `obleth.objectStorage.bucket` | The bucket's name. Setting it turns the object store on |
| `OBLETH_S3_ENDPOINT` | `obleth.objectStorage.endpoint` | The store's URL, such as `https://s3.example.edu:9021`; unset for AWS S3. Requests use path-style addresses |
| `OBLETH_S3_REGION` | `obleth.objectStorage.region` | Signing region; default `us-east-1` |
| `OBLETH_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `OBLETH_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `obleth.objectStorage.existingSecret` | A key that may put, get and delete objects in the bucket; in Helm, a Secret holding both |
| `OBLETH_BATCH_RETENTION` | `obleth.batches.retention` | How long a batch and its answers are kept after it ends, as `<n>h` or `<n>d`; default `24h` |

```yaml
obleth:
  objectStorage:
    enabled: true
    endpoint: https://s3.example.edu:9021
    bucket: obleth
    existingSecret: obleth-s3   # OBLETH_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID

chunks.title: Batches
chunks.heading: Who sees a batch
chunks.text:
By default a batch and its files belong to the key that created them: another key, even in the same tenant, gets `404`. `OBLETH_BATCH_SCOPE=tenant` lets every key of a tenant see and manage the tenant's batches. A disabled key or an inactive tenant pauses its batches instead of failing them; they carry on when it is active again, unless the deadline passes first.

Operators see every tenant's batches on the dashboard's [Batches page](/docs/dashboard/control-plane#batches), and through the [management API](/docs/reference/management-api#batches).

The input file is written to the bucket in 4 MiB objects as it arrives, so an upload doesn't grow a gateway's memory with its size. Creating the batch reads it once and writes one Postgres row per request, holding the request's place in the file, not the request.

Every gateway replica runs a batch runner. A runner claims requests with a lease, keeps a few waiting for a background slot per batch owner and model beyond those running (so fairshare decides between owners by weight), and claims again as soon as one finishes. It reads each request from the bucket and sends it through the pipeline in process, as the batch's key, then stores the answer as one object before it marks the request done. Up to `OBLETH_BATCH_RUNNER_CONCURRENCY` (64) batch requests run at once per replica; `OBLETH_BATCH_RUNNER=false` stops a replica from running batches while it still serves the API.

A replica that shuts down stops claiming, lets its running requ

chunks.title: Conversations and sessions
chunks.heading: Derived ids
chunks.text:
With no id from the client, the gateway hashes the tenant, the leading system or developer messages and the first user message. That opening is resent unchanged on every turn, so the id stays the same for the whole conversation. Up to 8 KiB of the system and developer text is hashed, and up to 8 KiB of the first user message on top, so agents that share one long system prompt are still told apart by their first message. Requests with no `messages`, such as embeddings, get no derived id.

Derivation is on by default. Set `OBLETH_SESSION_ID_DERIVATION=false` to record only ids clients send.

Two separate conversations that open with the same system prompt and first message get the same derived id. When that matters, as with agents or shared front ends, send your own id.

chunks.title: Conversations and sessions
chunks.heading: Find a session in Request logs
chunks.text:
Open a request in Request logs. Its panel shows **Session** and **Session came from**: *the client* or *derived by the gateway*. Choose **This session** to list every request with that id, or type `session:<id>` in the search box.

![A request's panel in Request logs, showing its Session id, "derived by the gateway" under Session came from, and the This session button](/dashboard/request.png)

The id is also on each usage row in ClickHouse (`session_id` and `session_id_source`), so you can sum a conversation's tokens and cost; see [ClickHouse usage](/docs/reference/clickhouse-usage). `GET /api/v1/usage/logs` filters on `session_id`. On traces the root span carries `session.id` and `session.id.source`; see [Observability](/docs/operate/observability).

chunks.title: Conversations and sessions
chunks.heading: Keep a session on one replica
chunks.text:
Set a model's endpoint selection mode to `session_hash` and each session goes to the same backend endpoint, chosen by a consistent hash of its id, so it keeps hitting the replica whose prompt cache is already warm. A request with no session id falls back to load balancing. See [Reliability and failover](/docs/operate/reliability).

When agent sessions compete for too few slots, [session affinity](/docs/how-it-works/fairshare-engine#session-affinity) also lets a warm session's next step go first, so its prompt cache is still there when it runs.

chunks.title: Conversations and sessions
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
`x-obleth-session-id: <your id>` on each request
  The gateway derives an id from the conversation's opening
  Request logs, `session:<id>`

A chat conversation is many requests, one per turn. The gateway gives each request a session id so the turns can be grouped afterwards. You don't have to change your client for this, but a client that sends its own id controls the grouping exactly.

chunks.title: Conversations and sessions
chunks.heading: Send a session id
chunks.text:
Send the same id on every request of a conversation:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-obleth-session-id: conv-abc123" \
  -d '{"model": "qwen3-235b", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "continue our chat"}]}'
```

The gateway takes the first of these that is present and not empty:

| Order | Source |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `x-obleth-session-id` header |
| 2 | `x-session-id` header |
| 3 | `session_id` in the JSON body |
| 4 | `metadata.session_id` in the JSON body |
| 5 | `prompt_cache_key` in the JSON body (OpenAI's prompt cache key) |
| 6 | Derived by the gateway (see below) |

Values are trimmed and cut to 200 characters. The OpenAI `user` field is not a session source; it names an end user, not a conversation. Session headers are forwarded to the backend like any other header, and a body `session_id` stays in the body.

On `/v1/messages` the Anthropic `metadata` object is not carried over, so use a header there. Claude Code's own `x-claude-code-session-id` header is not read as a session id.

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: Identity keys
chunks.text:
Identity keys have no secret, so there is nothing to copy or rotate. **Disable** one to block that user at once, ahead of the token's expiry. Deleting one only resets it: the user's next token recreates it with fresh budgets. Anything scoped to a key is scoped to the user, such as [who can see a video job](/docs/clients/video-generation#who-can-see-a-job).

The Management API returns `kind`, `identity_issuer`, `identity_subject` and `identity_claims` on each key; join external account systems on `identity_subject`. Request logs show the `device_id` of identity-key traffic, and `GET /api/v1/usage/logs` filters on `device_id`.

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: Issuer settings
chunks.text:
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issuer` | required | Must equal the token's `iss` exactly |
| `audience` | required | Must appear in the token's `aud` |
| `tenant` | required | The tenant identity keys are created under |
| `jwks_url` | discovered | The key document. Without it, `jwks_uri` is read from `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` at startup |
| `algorithms` | `["RS256", "ES256"]` | Allowed signing algorithms. Asymmetric only; `HS*` stops the gateway at startup |
| `subject_claim` | `sub` | The claim that names the user |
| `device_claim` | none | A claim recorded as `device_id` on usage rows (letters, digits, `_`, `-`; up to 64 characters) |
| `identity_claims` | `[]` | Extra claims stored on the identity key when it is created |
| `jit_provision` | `true` | Create the identity key on first use. With `false`, unknown users get 401 |

If the named tenant does not exist, it is created with default policy and an alert is raised. Where your account system already manages that tenant, treat the alert as a misconfiguration.

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
An OIDC provider, or an app that signs tokens and publishes a JWKS
  `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS`, then restart the gateway
  An identity key under the tenant you name

A caller sends the token wherever an API key goes: `Authorization: Bearer …` or `x-api-key`. The gateway verifies it offline against the issuer's published public keys (JWKS), maps the issuer and subject to an **identity key**, and from then on treats the request like one made with a key: tenant status, schedules, budgets, model allowlists and guardrails all apply. This works on every data-plane route, including `/v1/messages` and `/mcp/<server>`.

The token must be a signed compact JWT. A provider that issues opaque access tokens, such as Globus Auth, can't be used this way: the gateway reads an opaque token as an API key and refuses it. obleth-chat users don't need this either way, because by default [Chat signs its own tokens](/docs/run-chat/connect-gateway) for each person.

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: Rotating the signing key
chunks.text:
The gateway refreshes each issuer's keys every 15 minutes, and a token with an unknown `kid` triggers at most one extra fetch a minute. If a refresh fails, the previous keys keep working.

1. Generate a new keypair with a new `kid`.
2. Publish both public keys and wait for the gateway to fetch them.
3. Sign new tokens with the new key.
4. Remove the old public key once every token it signed has expired.

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: Troubleshooting
chunks.text:
Every verification failure returns 401 `invalid token`. A verified user whose key cannot be created gets 503 `identity provisioning unavailable`. Read the reason from the metrics port:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics | grep obleth_jwt
```

| `obleth_jwt_verify_total{result}` | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `unknown_issuer` | `iss` matches no configured issuer. Compare exactly, trailing slash included |
| `bad_alg` | The header's `alg` is not allowed for this issuer |
| `unknown_kid` | No `kid`, or no loaded key has it |
| `bad_signature` | The key with that `kid` did not verify the token |
| `expired`, `not_yet_valid` | Outside `exp` or `nbf`; check clock drift |
| `bad_audience` | `aud` is missing or lacks the configured audience |
| `bad_subject` | The subject claim is missing, empty or not a string |
| `malformed` | Not a parseable JWT, or over 8,192 bytes |
| `not_provisioned` | Verified, but unknown and `jit_provision` is `false` |
| `provision_failed` | Verified, but the key could not be created (503, and an alert) |

`not_provisioned` and `provision_failed` are counted as well as `ok`. If no counter moves at all, the credential never reached the verifier: the feature is off, or the value does not look like a JWT. `obleth_jwks_refresh_total{issuer_index, result}` counts key-document fetches; a steady `error` rate means tokens signed by any newly rotated key will fail.

Anyone can generate a keypair, but the gateway trusts only the keys in the JWKS documents of

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: Turn it on
chunks.text:
Set `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` to a JSON array with one entry per issuer you trust:

```json
[
  {
    "issuer": "https://idp.example.com",
    "audience": "obleth",
    "tenant": "cli-users",
    "algorithms": ["ES256"],
    "device_claim": "device_id",
    "identity_claims": ["uid"]
  }
]
```

On Kubernetes, set `obleth.jwtIssuers` in your values. With `obleth.existingSecret`, put the JSON under the `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` key of that Secret. On Compose, set it in `deploy/docker/.env`.

The variable is read once, at startup. On Compose, run `docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml up -d obleth`. The Helm chart rolls the pods when its own Secret changes; after editing an existing Secret, roll the deployment yourself.

```
INFO obleth: jwks loaded issuer=https://idp.example.com
INFO obleth: jwt bearer auth enabled issuers=1
```

Neither line means the variable is empty, and every credential is treated as an API key. `jwks not loaded at boot` means the key document could not be fetched; that issuer's tokens fail until a refresh succeeds. An invalid configuration stops the gateway from starting.

```bash
curl -s https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "my-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "ping"}]}'
```

A 200 means the token verified and the user's identity key exists. It shows on the API Keys page as `identity · <subject>`. A 401 carries no detail; see [Tro

chunks.title: Identity tokens
chunks.heading: What a token must carry
chunks.text:
- A compact JWS (three base64url parts starting `eyJ`) of at most 8,192 bytes. Anything else is looked up as an API key.
- A header `alg` from the issuer's `algorithms`, and a `kid`. Keys are looked up by `kid` alone.
- `iss` and `aud` matching the issuer entry, a non-empty string subject, and `exp`. `nbf` and `iat` are checked when present, with 60 seconds of clock skew.

If your provider is a full OIDC server (Keycloak, Okta, Entra, Auth0, Dex), create a client whose audience is the configured value and you are done. If you sign tokens yourself, generate an ES256 or RS256 keypair, keep the private key in your own secret store, publish the public key with a `kid` at an unauthenticated JWKS URL, and sign short-lived tokens (minutes to hours) with `iss`, `aud`, `sub` and `exp`. The gateway never receives the private key.

Whoever holds the signing key can mint a token for any subject, and with `jit_provision` on the gateway creates a key for it. Protect it like the admin token.

chunks.title: MCP gateway
chunks.heading: Add a server
chunks.text:
On the MCP servers page, choose **Add server** and fill in **Name**, **Upstream URL** and, if the server needs one, **Authorization** (the full header value, such as `Bearer ghp_…`). **Add and check** saves it and checks it at once.

The name is the path clients use (`/mcp/github`) and the name models are granted it by: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, up to 64 characters, starting with a letter or digit.

The page checks every server when it opens: whether it answers, its tools, the models that use it, its calls in the last 7 days and its response time. A server that does not answer shows under **Not answering**. See [Verifying a server](#verifying-a-server).

Open the server and turn on the models under **Models that can use it**. Only models with Function calling on are listed. Then turn on the tool loop so the gateway runs the calls (see [below](#the-gateway-tool-loop)).

If clients should call the server themselves at `/mcp/<server>`, open it and pick their tenants under **Tenants that can call it directly**. Keys of any other tenant get 403. Leave the list empty for a server that only models use.

Or use the Management API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/mcp-servers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "github", "upstream_url": "https://mcp.githubcopilot.com/mcp", "auth_header": "Bearer ghp_…", "allowed_tenants": ["<tenant id>"]}'
```

`GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/mcp-server

chunks.title: MCP gateway
chunks.heading: Call a server through the gateway
chunks.text:
Point the MCP client at the gateway with a gateway key:

```
POST https://gateway.example.com/mcp/github
Authorization: Bearer sk_...
Content-Type: application/json

{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "tools/list", "id": 1}
```

The key may also go in `x-api-key`, and an [identity token](/docs/clients/identity-tokens) works as it does for model traffic. For each call the gateway:

1. Authenticates the credential and applies the tenant gate: a disabled key, a tenant that is not active, or one outside its activation window, expiry or weekly schedule gets 403.
2. Looks up the server; a disabled one gets 403 `mcp server is disabled`, and one not opened to the key's tenant gets 403 `this key's tenant may not use this mcp server`.
3. Counts the call against the key's limit of 600 calls a minute to that server; past it the call gets 429 with `Retry-After`.
4. Removes the client's credential, cookies and forwarded-address headers, and sends the server's Authorization header instead. Clients never see it.
5. Forwards the request and streams the answer back, JSON or SSE. Only the response headers MCP uses come back: content type, `mcp-session-id`, `mcp-protocol-version`, `WWW-Authenticate`, `Retry-After` and cache control. A server cannot set cookies or grant cross-origin access from the gateway's address.

The gateway does not parse JSON-RPC, so any MCP-over-HTTP server works. `/mcp/<server>/<rest>` forwards the rest of the path and the query string. Bodies are limited to 16 MiB. MCP calls

chunks.title: MCP gateway
chunks.heading: Errors
chunks.text:
| Status | Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid request path` | The sub-path tries to leave the server's path |
| 401 | `missing bearer token`, `invalid api key`, `invalid token` | No credential, or one that does not verify |
| 403 | `api key disabled`, `tenant is not active`, or a schedule reason | The key or tenant may not call now |
| 403 | `mcp server is disabled` | The server is turned off |
| 403 | `this key's tenant may not use this mcp server` | The server is not opened to the key's tenant |
| 404 | `mcp server '<name>' is not registered` | No server by that name |
| 413 | `request body too large` | Over 16 MiB |
| 429 | `too many calls to this mcp server; try again shortly` | The key made 600 calls to this server in the last minute; sends `Retry-After` |
| 502 | `mcp upstream request failed` | The server could not be reached |
| 503 | `authentication backend unavailable`, `identity provisioning unavailable` | The credential lookup failed |

An error status from the server itself, 5xx included, is passed back unchanged.

`obleth_mcp_requests_total{server, status}` counts calls per server by status class (`2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`). With tracing on, each call is an `mcp_request` span tagged with the server name. Per-server daily counts (direct calls, tool-loop calls, failures, time) feed the MCP servers page and `GET /api/v1/stats/daily?kind=mcp`.

These alerts go to your alert channels (see [Alerting](/docs/operate/alerting)): `mcp_upstream_request_faile

chunks.title: MCP gateway
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
`/mcp/<server>` on the data plane, any method
  A streamable-HTTP or SSE MCP server
  MCP servers › Add server
  Keys of the tenants named for the server, while the tenant is active and in its schedule

A registered MCP server is used two ways. Clients with a key of a tenant you name for the server call it directly at `/mcp/<server>`, and the gateway adds the server's own credential on the way. Models you grant it to get its tools, and the gateway runs their tool calls for them. A new server is open to no tenant: until you name some, only the models granted its tools use it.

chunks.title: MCP gateway
chunks.heading: The gateway tool loop
chunks.text:
When a model is granted MCP servers and the tool loop is on, a plain chat client gets a grounded answer without ever seeing a tool. The gateway adds the servers' tools to the request, runs the model's tool calls against the servers, feeds back the results and asks again until the model answers. A client that sends its own `tools` keeps them: the granted tools are merged in, and only the gateway's own calls are run by the gateway.

To use it: register the server, grant it to a model with Function calling on, and turn on **Tool loop** in Settings › Boons, then save. Turn limits, per-tool timeout, the per-request deadline and billing are covered in [Boons](/docs/boons/overview).

chunks.title: MCP gateway
chunks.heading: Verifying a server
chunks.text:
A wrong URL or a rejected credential only shows when something calls the server, so the dashboard runs the real MCP handshake (`initialize`, then `tools/list`) through `/mcp/<name>`. It uses its own operator key, which reaches every server whichever tenants it is opened to. It does this when the MCP servers page opens, when you add a server, and when you choose **Check again**. It reports whether the server answered, its name and version, its tools and the round-trip time. These checks are not counted in the server's call statistics.

The [Playground assistant](/docs/dashboard/playground) can check every registered server, or a named few, in one step and returns a pass or fail row per server.

chunks.title: 3D mesh generation
chunks.heading: In the Playground
chunks.text: The Playground's [3D](/docs/dashboard/playground#3d) mode takes an image (choose, drop or paste one, or send a generated picture from Image mode), shows the job's stage and progress, and opens the finished model in a viewer you can turn around, with a download button.

chunks.title: 3D mesh generation
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A backend that serves the mesh job API below
  Register the model with `model_type: "mesh"`
  A flat price per created job (`cost_per_video`)
  The key that created it, by default

A mesh model turns a picture of an object into a textured 3D model. Like a video, a mesh takes minutes, so it is a job: the create call returns a job id at once, the backend works in the background, and the client polls the job until it can download the model as binary glTF (`.glb`).

```
POST   /v1/meshes               create a job (an image, optional settings)
GET    /v1/meshes/{id}          job status, as the backend reports it
GET    /v1/meshes/{id}/content  the finished model (model/gltf-binary)
DELETE /v1/meshes/{id}          delete the job
GET    /v1/meshes               the caller's own jobs
```

The gateway handles mesh jobs exactly like [video jobs](/docs/clients/video-generation): the same ownership, routing, billing and retention, with its own path. A mesh job is only ever found through `/v1/meshes`; its id sent to `/v1/videos` is a 404, and the other way round.

chunks.title: 3D mesh generation
chunks.heading: Ownership, billing and limits
chunks.text:
Everything in [Video generation](/docs/clients/video-generation) applies, with `mesh` in place of `video`:

- **Who can see a job** follows `OBLETH_VIDEO_JOB_SCOPE` (`key` by default, or `tenant`). A job id you don't own returns 404 `no such mesh job`, the same as an id that never existed.
- **Billing.** A create is charged the model's per-job price once the backend accepts the job and the gateway has recorded it, as request type `mesh`. Polls, downloads, deletes and listings are free and write no usage row.
- **Admission.** The create takes a slot in the model's pool only while the create call runs, so fairshare limits how fast jobs are created, not how many run at once. A backend with a queue limit can answer `429`, which passes through.
- **Records** share the job table and its retention (`OBLETH_VIDEO_JOB_RETENTION_HOURS`), with the job's kind recorded on each row.
- **Health.** Mesh models get no generation probe; the check is whether the backend's catalog lists them. `GET /v1/models` reports them as `model_type: "mesh"`.

The input image is not scanned by [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails), and a multipart create is sent once and never retried.

chunks.title: 3D mesh generation
chunks.heading: Run a job
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "image-to-3d",
    "model_type": "mesh",
    "upstream_model": "my-mesh-model",
    "api_base": "https://mesh.example.internal/v1",
    "api_key": "the-backend-token",
    "cost_per_video": 0.20,
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`api_base` ends in `/v1`; the gateway appends `/meshes`. Mesh models share the flat per-job price field with video models, so the price goes in `cost_per_video`; the model's form on the Models page labels it **Per mesh**.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/meshes \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -F model=image-to-3d -F image=@chair.png -F seed=42
```

The response is the backend's own job object.

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/meshes/$MESH_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY"
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/meshes/$MESH_ID/content -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" -o chair.glb
curl -s -X DELETE http://localhost:8088/v1/meshes/$MESH_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY"
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/meshes -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY"
```

In Python:

```python
import os
import time
import requests

url = "http://localhost:8088/v1/meshes"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OBLETH_KEY']}"}

with open("chair.png", "rb") as image:
    job = requests.post(url, headers=headers, files={"image": image}, data={"model

chunks.title: 3D mesh generation
chunks.heading: What the backend serves
chunks.text:
There is no OpenAI standard for 3D, so the gateway asks little of the backend:

- `POST {api_base}/meshes` accepts `multipart/form-data` (the image as a file field) or JSON, and answers with a JSON object whose `id` is the job id.
- `GET {api_base}/meshes/{id}` and `GET {api_base}/meshes/{id}/content` return the job and the file. While the job runs, the download may answer any not-ready status; it is passed through.
- `DELETE {api_base}/meshes/{id}` removes the job.
- `GET {api_base}/meshes` returns `{"data": [...]}` with an `id` and `created_at` on each job. The gateway keeps only the caller's entries, so a backend may list every job it holds.

Which settings a create takes (resolution, face count, texture size, seed) and the statuses a job goes through are the backend's; the gateway does not check them. A backend that is reachable directly can require the model's upstream key on every call, so that only the gateway can use it.

chunks.title: Model load
chunks.heading: Ask for the load
chunks.text:
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/load -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "scope": "cluster",
  "data": [
    {"id": "llama-3-70b", "state": "busy", "slots": 40, "in_flight": 34, "waiting": 0,
     "you": {"in_flight": 2, "limit": 4}},
    {"id": "qwen3-8b", "state": "free", "slots": 32, "in_flight": 3, "waiting": 0,
     "you": {"in_flight": 0, "limit": 4}}
  ]
}
```

`data` has one entry for each id the caller's [`GET /v1/models`](/docs/clients/openai-compatible-api#model-discovery) lists, sorted by id, so a tenant with a model list sees only its own models. Add `?model=<id>` for one entry; an id the caller is not offered returns `404` `model '<id>' not found`.

Each entry describes its model's [pool](/docs/sharing/how-fairshare-works#each-model-has-its-own-pool), the same numbers the dashboard's Fairshare page shows. A [variant](/docs/models/model-variants) shares its model's pool, and a family reports its default member's.

chunks.title: Model load
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
`GET /v1/load`, on the same port as chat
  The caller's own key or identity token
  Nothing: no slot, no budget, no ledger row
  About a second

chunks.title: Model load
chunks.heading: Say why a request waits
chunks.text:
- **The pool is full.** With `waiting` above `0`, a new request queues behind the others and gets a slot by [fair share](/docs/sharing/how-fairshare-works#who-gets-the-next-slot), within `OBLETH_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default `60`) or a `503`.
- **The caller is at its own cap.** `you.in_flight` at `you.limit` means the caller's next request to that model waits for one of its own there to finish, even while the pool has free slots. A tenant's cap counts all of its keys together, so a request can also wait below `limit` when other keys of the tenant are busy.
- **The model is offline.** It has no API base, no enabled endpoint, or a watched backend with no ready replica.

A key with [per-end-user fairshare](/docs/sharing/one-key-many-people) counts the end user named in `x-obleth-end-user` as `you`, the way its requests queue. Without the header, `you` counts the key's requests that name no end user.

Each gateway replica reads the pools at most once a second and shares that reading among every caller, so many clients can poll every few seconds. A successful answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

In shared slot mode, `in_flight` is read from the cluster-wide slot counts, which include the gateway's own health checks. A model registered less than a second ago can read `offline` until the next reading.

`OBLETH_LOAD_ENDPOINT=false` (Helm `obleth.loadEndpoint`) turns the endpoint off; the path then answers `404` `unknown endpoint`. If the fairshare scheduler does not answer,

chunks.title: Model load
chunks.heading: What the fields mean
chunks.text:
| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `slots` | Requests the pool runs at once: the model's max in flight, its [discovered size](/docs/models/pool-sizes), or `OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT`. `0` when the model has nowhere to send a request |
| `in_flight` | Requests running in the pool |
| `waiting` | Requests queued for a slot in the pool |
| `state` | `free`; `busy` when at least 80% of the slots are in use; `full` when every slot is in use or any request is waiting; `offline` when `slots` is `0` |
| `scope` | `cluster` when the counts cover every gateway replica; `replica` when they are the answering replica's own: its share of each pool and its requests, as when slots are not shared or Redis is not answering |
| `you` | Only when the caller's key or tenant has a max in flight: the caller's own requests in this pool |
| `you.in_flight` | The caller's own requests running in this entry's pool |
| `you.limit` | The lower of the key's and the tenant's max in flight. It holds in each model's pool separately, so it is the same on every entry |

The answer never names or counts another tenant's or key's requests on their own; they are only part of a pool's totals.

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Discovery
chunks.text:
`GET /v1/models` reports each model's `model_type` and `mode` (where `image` is `image_generation` and `video` is `video_generation`), so a client can group models by what they do. See [Model discovery](/docs/clients/openai-compatible-api#model-discovery).

Health probes send a minimal real request to the route the type serves: a one-token chat call, an embedding of `ping`, a speech request for `.`, or a transcription of 0.1 seconds of silence. Image and video models get no generation probe, because it would cost a full render; the check is whether the backend's model catalog lists them, and a catalog the backend refuses with a 4xx leaves the model `unknown`, not `unhealthy`. See [Health checks](/docs/models/model-health).

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Embeddings
chunks.text:
```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8088/v1", api_key="sk_...")

resp = client.embeddings.create(model="qwen3-embedding-8b", input="The quick brown fox")
print(len(resp.data[0].embedding))
```

Embedding inputs go through the tenant's input [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails) like chat prompts do.

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Images
chunks.text:
Any backend that serves the OpenAI images API works, including Stable Diffusion servers that expose it. Backends with their own graph APIs, such as ComfyUI workflows, do not.

```python
img = client.images.generate(model="sdxl", prompt="a watercolor fox", n=2, size="1024x1024")
print(img.data[0].url)
```

Edits and variations send the source image as `multipart/form-data`. The gateway reads the form's `model` field, swaps in the model's `upstream_model` and forwards the file unchanged. `n` is read from the form (default 1). The form's `prompt` is scanned by input guardrails; the image is not.

```python
with open("photo.png", "rb") as image:
    result = client.images.edit(model="sdxl", image=image, prompt="make it a watercolor")
```

An `image` model can also answer chat users mid-conversation through the [image generation boon](/docs/boons/image-generation), and you can try it in the Playground's Image mode.

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: In the Playground
chunks.text: The Playground's **Speech** mode reads a pasted block of text aloud with any `audio_speech` model. It plays the audio as it arrives when the backend streams, and shows how long the first audio took, how fast the audio was made against real time, and what it cost. **Get code** gives the same call in curl, Python and JavaScript.

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
Register the model with its `model_type`
  Any server with the matching OpenAI endpoint
  Per image, per character or per token, set on the model

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Register the model
chunks.text:
Give the model the `model_type` for what it serves. The type decides which routes it answers, how its health is checked and how it is priced. It defaults to `chat`.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "sdxl",
    "model_type": "image",
    "upstream_model": "stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0",
    "api_base": "https://images.example.internal/v1",
    "cost_per_image": 0.02,
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

Set `api_base` to the backend's base URL ending in `/v1`, not a full endpoint URL: the gateway appends the client's path to it. Every other model field is in [Model registry](/docs/models/model-registry), and you can also use **Add model** on the Models page.

| `model_type` | Routes | Body | Priced by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chat` | `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions` | JSON | `input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token` |
| `embedding` | `/v1/embeddings` | JSON | `input_cost_per_token` |
| `image` | `/v1/images/generations` | JSON | `cost_per_image` × `n` |
| `image` | `/v1/images/edits`, `/v1/images/variations` | multipart | `cost_per_image` × `n` |
| `audio_transcription` | `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations` | multipart | Not charged (see below) |
| `audio_speech` | `/v1/audio/speech` | JSON | `cost_per_character` of `input` |
| `video` | `/v1/videos` | JSON or multipart | `cost_per_video`; see

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Speech-to-text
chunks.text:
Transcription and translation clients upload audio as `multipart/form-data`. Both routes are served by an `audio_transcription` model.

```python
with open("speech.wav", "rb") as f:
    result = client.audio.transcriptions.create(model="qwen3-asr", file=f)
print(result.text)
```

A model can carry `cost_per_audio_second`, which is stored and reported, but no per-second charge is applied to transcription requests in this release.

For a tenant whose guardrails policy blocks or redacts output, transcription and translation return 400, because the gateway cannot scan their output. Use a chat route for that tenant.

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Streaming
chunks.text:
The gateway passes audio through as the backend sends it, so a backend that streams speech can be heard while the rest is still being made. Ask for a format that plays in pieces: `pcm` or `wav` with `stream_format: "audio"` for raw bytes, or `stream_format: "sse"` (or `stream: true`) for OpenAI's `speech.audio.delta` and `speech.audio.done` events. A backend that does not stream sends the whole file when it is done, so the same request works with either.

```python
with client.audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create(
    model="my-tts", voice="tara", input=long_text,
    response_format="pcm", stream_format="audio",
) as response:
    for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
        player.write(chunk)  # 16-bit mono PCM at the backend's sample rate
```

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Text-to-speech
chunks.text:
`/v1/audio/speech` returns audio bytes and is charged `cost_per_character` for each character of `input`.

```python
audio = client.audio.speech.create(model="qwen3-tts", voice="alloy", input="Hello from obleth.")
audio.write_to_file("out.mp3")
```

chunks.title: Images, audio and speech
chunks.heading: Voices
chunks.text:
`GET /v1/audio/voices?model=<name>` returns the voices the model's backend offers, in the shape vLLM-Omni uses:

```bash
curl https://gateway.example.com/v1/audio/voices?model=my-tts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_API_KEY"
# {"voices": ["tara", "leo", ...], "uploaded_voices": []}
```

The gateway checks the key and the tenant's allowlist as it would for a speech request, then forwards the call. It costs nothing and writes no usage row. A backend without this route answers `404`; any voice name it accepts still works on `/v1/audio/speech`.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Authentication
chunks.text:
Every route except `GET /health` needs a credential, in either header:

```
Authorization: Bearer sk_…
x-api-key: sk_…
```

The credential is an [API key](/docs/sharing/tenants-and-keys) or a short-lived [identity token](/docs/clients/identity-tokens) from an issuer you trust. The admin token is for the Management API only; never send it to the data plane. Error bodies are listed in [Authentication](/docs/reference/authentication).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Errors
chunks.text:
Errors use the OpenAI envelope:

```json
{"error": {"message": "model 'llama-3-7b' is not registered", "type": "obleth_gateway_error"}}
```

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `model is required`, invalid JSON or multipart body, `stream must be true or false`, `invalid request path`, or a path this tenant's [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails) cannot enforce |
| 401 | `missing bearer token`, `invalid api key`, `invalid token` |
| 403 | The key or model is disabled, the tenant is not active or outside its schedule, the model is not in the tenant's allowlist, or a term budget is used up |
| 404 | `model '<name>' is not registered`, or `unknown endpoint` for a path or method the gateway does not forward |
| 410 | The model is retired; the body names the replacement (see [Model lifecycle](/docs/models/model-lifecycle#what-callers-see)) |
| 413 | The body is over 64 MiB |
| 429 | `token budget exceeded` (per-minute budget) |
| 503 | `timed out waiting for model capacity`, with `Retry-After: 5`; or `authentication backend unavailable` when the key lookup fails |

A 503 with `Retry-After` means the request waited in the model's queue for `OBLETH_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 60) without getting a slot. Retry after the delay, or see [How fairshare works](/docs/sharing/how-fairshare-works).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Headers
chunks.text:
The gateway reads these request headers:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `x-obleth-session-id`, `x-session-id` | Group requests into a session (see [Conversations and sessions](/docs/clients/conversations-and-sessions)) |
| `x-obleth-effort` | `low`, `medium` or `high`: difficulty for `model: "auto"`, ahead of the classifier |
| `x-obleth-boons` | `off` skips the model's boons for this request (tenant guardrails still run); `lossy` forces the compression boon's lossy pass |
| `x-obleth-end-user` | The person a shared key is serving, for a key with [per-user fairshare](/docs/sharing/one-key-many-people) |
| `x-obleth-classify-system` | Bytes at the end of the system text the `auto` classifier reads; `0` reads none (see [long system prompts](/docs/routing/auto-model-routing#long-system-prompts)) |

And adds these to responses:

| Header | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `x-obleth-request-id` | On every response. Search for it in Request logs |
| `x-obleth-queue-wait-ms` | How long the request waited in the queue before it went to the model, in milliseconds. Subtract it from the response time to see how long the model took |
| `x-obleth-boons` | The boons that ran, comma-separated |
| `x-obleth-boons-warning` | A boon hit a problem it recovered from |
| `x-obleth-cache` | `hit` when the [response cache](/docs/models/response-cache) answered |
| `x-obleth-compression` | `before=…;after=…;saved=…` token counts when compression ran |
| `x-obleth-model-variant` | The [variant](/docs

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Model discovery
chunks.text:
`GET /v1/models` lists every enabled model once, under the name clients call, straight from the gateway's registry, followed by each of its [variants](/docs/models/model-variants). It never calls a backend, so a model whose backend is down or has no catalog is still listed, and models a backend serves but the gateway has not registered are not. A tenant with a model allowlist sees only its own models.

Each entry has `id`, `object: "model"`, `owned_by: "obleth"`, `model_type`, `mode` (the LiteLLM spelling, where `image` is `image_generation` and `video` is `video_generation`), `quantization`, `tags`, `aliases`, the model's own `supports_*` flags, and its `boons` and `boon_details` (see [below](#the-models-own-abilities-and-its-boons)). A variant's entry adds `variant_of` and `description`, and its `boons` are its model's plus its own. [Staged and retired](/docs/models/model-lifecycle) models are left out, and a deprecated model's entry adds `status`, plus `replacement`, `retire_at` and `note` when set. Search tools are listed at [`GET /v1/search/tools`](/docs/clients/search-api) instead.

`GET /v1/models/{id}` returns the same entry for a name, alias or variant, and still answers for a retired model, so a caller can find its replacement. A staged model, or one outside the tenant's allowlist, returns 404.

`GET /model/info` adds prices, capability flags, context window, boons with their `boon_details`, variants, lifecycle `status` and last observed health. It never includes a

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The data-plane origin plus `/v1`, such as `http://localhost:8088/v1` on Compose
  A gateway key (`sk_…`) or an identity token
  `base_url` and `api_key`, nothing else

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Responses API
chunks.text:
`POST /v1/responses` becomes a chat request, runs through the same routing, admission, boons and billing, and comes back as a Responses object, streamed or not. Usage is recorded as request type `responses`.

- `instructions` becomes a leading system message, and `input` (a string, or `message`, `function_call` and `function_call_output` items) becomes the conversation.
- `max_output_tokens` becomes `max_tokens`, `text.format` becomes `response_format`, and `function` tools carry over. Hosted tools such as web search are dropped.
- The gateway stores no conversations. `store: true`, `previous_response_id` and `background: true` return 400; send the full conversation in `input` each time.
- Usage carries `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` when the backend reports cached prompt tokens; `input_tokens` stays the full count.
- The body limit is 32 MiB.

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Send a request
chunks.text:
Set the client's base URL to the gateway and its API key to a gateway key. The data-plane port is `8088` on the Compose host, `80` through the HAProxy edge profile, and `8080` when you run the gateway natively.

  
    curl
    Python
  
  

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama-3-70b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is obleth?"}],
    "max_tokens": 256
  }'
```

  
  

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8088/v1", api_key="sk_...")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="llama-3-70b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is obleth?"}],
    max_tokens=256,
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

  

The same settings work for LangChain's `ChatOpenAI`, the TypeScript `openai` package and any other OpenAI-compatible client. For Claude Code and the Anthropic SDKs, see [Claude Code and Anthropic SDKs](/docs/clients/anthropic-messages-api).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: Streaming
chunks.text:
Send `"stream": true` to get server-sent events. The gateway passes chunks to the client as they arrive and sets `x-accel-buffering: no` so an nginx-style proxy in front does not buffer them. The request keeps its place in the model's pool until the stream ends.

The gateway always asks the backend for token usage on the final chunk, because billing needs it. If your client did not ask for `stream_options.include_usage`, that extra chunk is removed before it reaches you.

When the backend reports prompt tokens served from its prefix cache in `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (vLLM does with `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`), chat responses pass it through and the usage ledger records it as `cached_input_tokens`.

A whole stream ends with a finish chunk, the usage chunk if you asked for it, and `[DONE]`. If the backend stops before that, you get one event in the error shape below, which OpenAI's SDKs raise as an `APIError`, and the stream ends without `[DONE]`. See [When a stream is cut short](/docs/reference/data-plane-routes#when-a-stream-is-cut-short).

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: The model's own abilities and its boons
chunks.text:
The `supports_*` flags describe the model itself. A [boon](/docs/boons/overview) is an ability the gateway adds, often by calling another model, so a result from a model with a boon can't be reproduced with that model alone. `boon_details` says, for each boon the model holds, whether it runs and which model does the work:

```json
{
  "id": "text-model",
  "supports_vision": false,
  "supports_function_calling": false,
  "boons": ["vision", "web_search"],
  "boon_details": {
    "vision": { "active": true, "native": false, "helper_model": "vision-model" },
    "web_search": { "active": false, "inactive_reason": "needs_function_calling" }
  }
}
```

This model can't see images. When a request has one, `vision-model` describes it and `text-model` answers from the description. Its `web_search` grant does nothing, because the model can't call tools.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `active` | The boon runs on the model's requests that call for it |
| `native` | Vision and structured output only: whether the model has the ability itself. If it does, the boon steps aside |
| `helper_model` | When active, the model or search tool that does the boon's work. Absent when no other model is involved: compression and knowledge run in the gateway, and structured output with no fixer asks the model itself to repair its reply |
| `inactive_reason` | When not active: `native`, `off` (off in Settings, or no helper picked), `needs_function_calling`, `no_collections`, `no_drafter` or `no_sco

chunks.title: OpenAI-compatible API
chunks.heading: What the gateway serves
chunks.text:
| Route | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | Chat, streaming or not, with every [boon](/docs/boons/overview) the model has |
| `POST /v1/completions` | Legacy text completions |
| `POST /v1/responses` | The Responses API, translated to chat and back (see [below](#responses-api)) |
| `POST /v1/embeddings` | Embeddings from an `embedding` model |
| `POST /v1/rerank`, `/v1/reranking` | Passed to the named model |
| `POST /v1/moderations` | Passed to the named model |
| `GET /v1/models`, `/v1/models/{id}` | Model discovery from the gateway's registry (see [below](#model-discovery)) |
| `GET /model/info`, `/v1/model/info` | Each model's configured facts |

Other surfaces have their own pages: [images, audio and speech](/docs/clients/multi-modal-models), [batches](/docs/clients/batches), [video jobs](/docs/clients/video-generation), [`/v1/messages`](/docs/clients/anthropic-messages-api), [`/v1/verdicts`](/docs/clients/verdicts), [`/v1/search`](/docs/clients/search-api) and [`/mcp/<server>`](/docs/clients/mcp-gateway). Every route and error message is in [Data-plane routes](/docs/reference/data-plane-routes).

The `model` field picks the model. A model's name and any of its [aliases](/docs/models/model-registry#aliases) both work, and usage is always recorded under the canonical name. A [variant](/docs/models/model-variants) name reaches the model with extra boons on. `model: "auto"` hands the choice to the [auto router](/docs/routing/auto-model-routing).

chunks.title: Search API
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
A search tool: a model of type `search` whose API base is a SearXNG instance
  `POST /v1/search`, or `POST /v1/search/{tool}`
  Nothing; logged as request type `search`

A client written for the Perplexity Search API, or for LiteLLM's `/v1/search`, which takes the same shape, works unchanged. The gateway runs each search through the JSON API of a [SearXNG](https://docs.searxng.org/) instance you run.

chunks.title: Search API
chunks.heading: Pick the search tool
chunks.text:
The tool comes from the path (`POST /v1/search/{tool}`), else the body's `search_tool_name`, else its `model`. With none of these, the caller's only search tool is used; with several, the request is refused and names `GET /v1/search/tools`, which lists the tools the key may use:

```json
{"object": "list", "data": [{"search_tool_name": "web", "search_provider": "searxng"}]}
```

The bare `/search`, `/search/{tool}` and `/search/tools` paths work too, as on LiteLLM.

chunks.title: Search API
chunks.heading: Register a search tool
chunks.text:
SearXNG answers JSON only when `json` is listed under `search.formats` in its settings. Without it, every search fails with a `403` from SearXNG.

On **Models**, add a model of type **Web search (SearXNG)** with the instance's root URL as the API base, not a `/v1` URL. Its name is the tool name clients send. On save, the dashboard runs a test search and warns if JSON output is off, and the model turns on once its first health check, also a real search, passes. If the instance needs credentials, set the model's API key (sent as a bearer token) or [upstream headers](/docs/models/model-registry#upstream-headers).

A tenant with a model allowlist needs the tool's name on it, like any model.

Or through the Management API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9180/api/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model_name": "web",
    "upstream_model": "searxng",
    "api_base": "http://searxng.example.internal:8080",
    "model_type": "search"
  }'
```

To try a tool from the dashboard, use the Playground's [Search](/docs/dashboard/playground#search) mode. To let chat models search, see the [Web search](/docs/boons/web-search) boon.

chunks.title: Search API
chunks.heading: Request fields
chunks.text:
| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `query` | Required. A string, or a list of strings searched as one, joined with spaces. At most 2,000 characters |
| `search_tool_name`, `model` | The search tool, when the path doesn't name it |
| `max_results` | 1 to 20. Results are cut to this many; without it, every result SearXNG returns |
| `search_domain_filter` | Up to 20 domains to keep results to. A domain covers its subdomains; `-domain` leaves it out instead. A single kept domain also adds `site:` to the query |
| `country` | A two-letter country code, turned into a SearXNG `language` for countries with one obvious search language, when `language` isn't set |
| `categories`, `engines`, `language`, `pageno`, `time_range`, `safesearch` | Passed to SearXNG. `categories` and `engines` also take a list |

LiteLLM ignores `max_results` and the domain filter; obleth applies both to the results after SearXNG answers.

chunks.title: Search API
chunks.heading: Search
chunks.text:
curl
    Python
  
  

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8088/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "search_tool_name": "web",
    "query": "postgres logical replication slots",
    "max_results": 5,
    "search_domain_filter": ["postgresql.org"]
  }'
```

  
  

```python
import os
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "http://localhost:8088/v1/search",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OBLETH_KEY']}"},
    json={
        "search_tool_name": "web",
        "query": "postgres logical replication slots",
        "max_results": 5,
        "search_domain_filter": ["postgresql.org"],
    },
)
for result in response.json()["results"]:
    print(result["title"], result["url"])
```

  

The response:

```json
{
  "id": "0b7e8f4a-6c1d-4c55-9a43-2f1d8e0c9b12",
  "object": "search",
  "results": [
    {
      "title": "Logical Replication",
      "url": "https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/logical-replication.html",
      "snippet": "Logical replication is a method of replicating data objects…",
      "date": null,
      "last_updated": null
    }
  ]
}
```

`id` is the request id, also sent as `x-obleth-request-id`. `snippet` is SearXNG's content for the result, and `date` its publication date when SearXNG has one, else `null`. `last_updated` is always `null`.

chunks.title: Search API
chunks.heading: What a search goes through
chunks.text:
A search takes the same path as a model call: key authentication, the tenant's model allowlist, the tenant's input [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails) (the query is scanned like a prompt, and a redacted query is searched as redacted), and [fairshare](/docs/sharing/how-fairshare-works) admission into the tool's own pool with no estimated tokens. It takes a slot, which protects the search upstream, but no share of anyone's tokens. Each search writes one usage row with `request_type: "search"` and no cost.

The call follows the tool's endpoints, moving on from one that is unreachable or answers 5xx. Its timeout is the model's request timeout, capped at 60 seconds. A tool can be [staged, deprecated or retired](/docs/models/model-lifecycle) like a model: a staged tool is not listed or picked by default, and a retired one is refused with `410` or answered by its replacement.

Search tools are not models. They are left out of `/v1/models` and `/model/info`, and a chat, embeddings or other request that names one gets `400` `'<name>' is a search tool: call POST /v1/search`.

| Status | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `request body must be a JSON object`, `query is required`, `query must not be empty`, `query is too long (maximum 2000 characters)`, `max_results must be an integer from 1 to 20`, `search_domain_filter takes at most 20 domains` |
| `400` | `search_tool_name is required: GET /v1/search/tools lists the choices`, when the key may use several tools |
| `400` | `'<name>'

chunks.title: Verdict examples
chunks.heading: Check a photo
chunks.text:
Send photos in `images` with any question type. The model must accept images; with `auto`, the router picks one that does.

```python
import base64
from pathlib import Path

def data_url(path):
    return "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(Path(path).read_bytes()).decode()

DAMAGE = {
    "visible_damage": {
        "type": "boolean",
        "instructions": "Is the phone's screen or body visibly damaged, such as cracked glass "
                        "or a dent? Ignore smudges, reflections and the case.",
    },
    "severity": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How badly is the phone damaged?",
        "criteria": [
            "No visible damage",
            "Scuffs or scratches only",
            "Cracked, but the screen is readable",
            "Shattered or unusable",
        ],
    },
}

v = verdicts("A customer's photo of the phone they are returning.", DAMAGE,
             model="auto", images=[data_url("returned-phone.jpg")])
if v["visible_damage"]["probabilities"]["true"] >= 0.9:
    print("damaged, severity", v["severity"]["value"])
```

| Photo | `visible_damage` | `severity` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screen shattered across its whole width | 1.00 | 4 |
| Screen cracked out from one point | 1.00 | 4 |
| An undamaged phone, held in a hand | 0.00 | 1 |

The `visible_damage` column is the probability of `true`. Each photo cost about 270 prompt tokens per question on this model.

chunks.title: Verdict examples
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
`POST /v1/verdicts`
  [Verdicts](/docs/clients/verdicts)
  Playground › Verdicts

The examples call a gateway at `http://localhost:8088` with the model `qwen3-8b`. Use any chat model on your gateway, or `auto`. The results shown come from running these requests against a 31B instruct model and are rounded; another model gives different numbers.

The Python examples share this helper:

```python
import os
import requests

def verdicts(state, questions, model="qwen3-8b", images=None):
    body = {"model": model, "state": state, "questions": questions}
    if images:
        body["images"] = images
    r = requests.post(
        "http://localhost:8088/v1/verdicts",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OBLETH_KEY']}"},
        json=body,
        timeout=120,
    )
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["verdicts"]
```

chunks.title: Verdict examples
chunks.heading: Set thresholds from labeled examples
chunks.text:
The thresholds above are placeholders. Run a question over a few hundred items your team has already labeled, and look at what each threshold would have caught.

```python
labeled = [
    ("Payouts have failed for three days and payroll runs tomorrow.", True),
    ("Could you add an export to Excel?", False),
    # ... a few hundred more
]
URGENT = {"is_urgent": {"type": "boolean", "instructions": "Does this need action today?"}}

results = [
    (verdicts(text, URGENT)["is_urgent"]["probabilities"]["true"], label)
    for text, label in labeled
]
positives = sum(label for _, label in results)

for t in (0.5, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99):
    flagged = [label for p, label in results if p >= t]
    precision = sum(flagged) / len(flagged) if flagged else 1.0
    recall = sum(flagged) / positives
    print(f"{t:.2f}  precision {precision:.2f}  recall {recall:.2f}  flagged {len(flagged)}")
```

Choose the threshold by what each mistake costs: a missed urgent ticket, or a false alarm. Probabilities shift between models and between wordings of a question, so run this again when you change either. Send answers with low `confidence` to a person, whatever their probability.

chunks.title: Verdict examples
chunks.heading: Write questions that work
chunks.text:
- Ask about something the state shows ("Does the report mention lost data?"), not a judgment the model has to invent ("Is this important?").
- Ask one thing per question. "Is it urgent, and is it about billing?" is a boolean and a choice.
- Give choices distinct meanings. When the options may not cover every state, add a fallback such as `other`, and send it to a person.
- List score levels lowest first, and make neighbouring levels differ in one clear way.
- Put definitions in `criteria`, not `instructions`. Each description is shown next to its option or level.
- Name options with the values your code switches on. The chosen name comes back as `value`.
- Ask every independent question about one state in one request, so the state is processed once.

chunks.title: Verdicts
chunks.heading: Admission and cost
chunks.text:
- The request is authenticated and checked like any other, including the tenant's model allowlist and input [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails), which scan the state and each question before admission.
- The whole request takes **one** slot in the model's pool, however many questions it has. An admission timeout returns 503 with `Retry-After: 5`.
- Budgets are reserved from an estimate (each image counts as 1,500 tokens per question) and settled once with the real usage, as one usage row with request type `verdict`. When a question fails, the calls that did run are still billed.
- With tracing on for the key, each question is a `verdict:q:<id>` span with its answer, confidence and token counts.
- Boons, output guardrails and the response cache do not apply.

To make a high-volume question set cheaper, a small model can be distilled from a large model's verdicts. See [Training a classifier](/docs/routing/training-a-model).

Errors use the OpenAI envelope, `{"error": {"message": "…", "type": "obleth_gateway_error"}}`.

| Status | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid JSON body`; `too many questions: 40 (maximum 32)`; `question 'x': a choice needs at least 2 options`; `too many images: 9 (maximum 8)`; `model 'x' does not accept images; use a model with vision`; `verdicts requires a chat model; 'x' is registered as 'embedding'`; `request blocked by content policy` |
| 401 | `missing bearer token`; `invalid api key`; `invalid token` |
| 403 | `model is disabled`; `model not
