**Helm with `obleth.existingSecret`: add the new keys to the Secret first.** The chart now reads the Redis URL from the Secret, because it carries the Redis password, instead of setting it in the pod environment. With `existingSecret` the chart does not render that Secret. If a key is missing, the new pods cannot start (the gateway has no Redis URL, and the bundled Redis and Postgres have no password) and the rollout stalls, with the old pods still serving. Before upgrading:

- **External Redis** (`redis.enabled: false`): copy the URL the running pods use into the Secret. It must include the password if your Redis requires one.

  ```bash
  kubectl patch secret <existing-secret> -n <namespace> --type merge -p "{\"stringData\":{\"OBLETH_REDIS_URL\":\"$(kubectl get deploy <release>-obleth -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.name=="OBLETH_REDIS_URL")].value}')\"}}"
  ```

- **Bundled Redis** (`redis.enabled: true`): the upgraded Redis requires a password, so the URL the running pods use (which has none) will not authenticate. Generate a password and add it together with a URL that carries it:

  ```bash
  PW=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
  kubectl patch secret <existing-secret> -n <namespace> --type merge -p "{\"stringData\":{\"REDIS_PASSWORD\":\"$PW\",\"OBLETH_REDIS_URL\":\"redis://:$PW@<release>-redis:6379\"}}"
  ```

- **Bundled Postgres** (`postgres.enabled: true`

chunks.title: Upgrading from v1.x
chunks.heading: Other changes in v2.0.0
chunks.text:
v2.0.0 also changes behaviour that needs no action, such as `503` instead of `401` when Redis fails during a key lookup, and `GET /v1/models` listing the gateway's registry. Read the [release notes](https://github.com/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) before upgrading.

Rolling back across v2.0.0 returns Redis to running without a password; migrations are not reverted.

- **v0.5.0:** the dashboard signs in by email. Set `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` to a real address and `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` to at least 8 characters first, or no admin is created.
- **v0.9.4:** remove `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_RESTART_AFTER_FAILURES=3` if you set it; the default is `20`.

chunks.title: Upgrading from v1.x
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
An install still on a v1.x release
  The steps below, before the new pods start
  Upgrade as in [Upgrades](/docs/operate/upgrades)

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
One chart version bump carries every image
  Set `OBLETH_VERSION`, pull, recreate
  Migrates itself at start-up
  What changes in v2.12.0, below

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Roll back
chunks.text:
```bash
helm rollback obleth <previous-revision> -n obleth
```

Migrations are not reverted, but the older gateway ignores columns it does not read. A v2.11.x gateway cannot use the batch tables migration `0046` reshaped, so its `/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` requests fail until you upgrade again; other traffic is unaffected. A v2.6.x gateway ignores `allowed_networks` and `background`, so a limited key works from any network and a background key competes as interactive traffic, and it records no client addresses. A v2.4.x gateway ignores `allowed_tenants`, so every enabled MCP server is open to direct calls from any key again; it forwards other paths to a model's upstream as before; and it has no batches, so running batches stop until you upgrade again, with what they had finished kept. Before rolling back from v2.4.0, turn session affinity off on the gateway and on every model, and let the hold time (3 seconds by default, at most 60) pass so no slot is still held: an older gateway counts a held slot against its pool and never frees it. A v2.3.x gateway ignores per-model session affinity and keeps no conversation on its model. A v2.2.x gateway also has no mesh jobs or rejected request fields. A v2.1.x gateway has no reasoning maps or model families: it passes effort through, answers a family's name as an unknown model, and lists unlisted models. A v2.0.x gateway also has no model lifecycle, so it serves staged, deprecated and retired models as active.

The chart version has n

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Upgrade with Docker Compose
chunks.text:
Update your checkout of `deploy/docker/` to the release first (for example `git checkout v2.10.0`), so the Compose files match it, then pull and recreate:

```bash
OBLETH_VERSION=v2.12.0 docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml pull
OBLETH_VERSION=v2.12.0 docker compose -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate
```

From v2.12.0 the compressor image follows `OBLETH_VERSION` too; remove an `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION` you set for an earlier release. There is no rolling upgrade: the old gateway drains for up to 345 seconds first.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: Upgrade with Helm
chunks.text:
```bash
helm upgrade obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth --version 2.10.0 \
  -n obleth --reset-then-reuse-values --dry-run | grep 'image:'
```

Every image should end in `:v2.10.0`. Image tags default to the chart's version, so one chart upgrade moves every component.

```bash
helm upgrade obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth \
  --version 2.10.0 \
  --namespace obleth \
  --reset-then-reuse-values \
  --wait
```

`--reset-then-reuse-values` (Helm 3.14+) takes the new chart's defaults and re-applies the values you set. `--wait` fails the upgrade if the new pods do not become ready.

```bash
helm history obleth -n obleth | tail -2
kubectl -n obleth get pods
kubectl -n obleth logs deploy/obleth-obleth -c obleth --tail=25
```

The log shows `postgres connected + schema applied`, `redis connected`, `clickhouse connected + schema applied` (or `telemetry started in spill mode`) and `listening: proxy=…`. Settings › About shows the running version.

Migrations run by themselves at every start, under a lock so replicas cannot race, and only add tables and columns, so old and new pods run side by side. v2.10.0 and v2.9.0 add none, v2.8.0 added `0044`, v2.7.0 `0042` and `0043`, v2.6.0 added `0041`, v2.5.0 `0039` and `0040`, v2.4.0 `0038`, v2.3.0 `0036` and `0037`, v2.2.0 `0035`, and v2.1.0 `0031` to `0034`; see [Postgres schema](/docs/reference/postgres-schema).

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changed in v2.1.0
chunks.text:
Read this too when you upgrade from v2.0.x. There is nothing to do before upgrading from v2.0.x: no new required values or Secret keys, and every schema change is additive, so old and new pods run side by side. Coming from v1.x, first follow [Upgrading from v1.x](/docs/operate/upgrade-from-v1).

**Applied at startup.**

- Postgres migrations `0031` to `0034`: the Slurm launch history, [per-user fairshare](/docs/sharing/one-key-many-people) on keys, model [variants](/docs/models/model-variants) and the model [lifecycle](/docs/models/model-lifecycle). Every existing model starts active. While a rollout is in progress, an older gateway serves a staged model as active.
- ClickHouse columns on `usage`: `cached_input_tokens`, `end_user`, `parent_request_id` and `model_variant`, added in place. `usage_daily` is unchanged, and rows the older version spilled to its WAL replay with zero or empty values.

**The bundled ClickHouse keeps a week of its own logs.** The chart's `clickhouse.systemLogRetentionDays` (7) and `clickhouse.logLevel` (`information`), and Compose's `clickhouse/system-logs.xml`, bound the server's system log tables, which the stock image keeps forever. The ClickHouse pod restarts once; meanwhile the gateway spills usage to its write-ahead log and replays it. On that first start, ClickHouse renames each system log table to `<name>_0` and starts a fresh one; the old tables keep their data until you drop them:

```sql
SELECT name, formatReadableSize(total_bytes) FROM sys

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changed in v2.2.0
chunks.text:
Read this too when you upgrade from v2.1.x. There is nothing to do before upgrading from v2.1.x: no new required values or Secret keys, and every schema change is additive, so old and new pods run side by side. Coming from v2.0.x, also read the v2.1.0 section below.

**Applied at startup.**

- Postgres migration `0035`: [reasoning effort](/docs/models/reasoning-effort) maps and the listing switch on `models`, and the `model_families` table. Every existing model keeps passing effort through as sent and stays listed.
- ClickHouse columns on `usage`: `reasoning_effort`, `reasoning_effort_requested` and `model_family`, added in place. A call through a model family now records the family in `model_family`; `model_variant` holds real variants only.

**The compressor follows `image.tag`.** The chart's `compressor.image.tag` and `compressor.image.pullPolicy` now default to `image.tag` and `image.pullPolicy`, like every other component. A release install is unchanged. An install that sets `image.tag` to `dev` or `main` now runs the edge compressor too, which edge builds publish from this release on. Set `compressor.image.tag` to keep it on its own tag.

**Behaviour that needs no action:**

- A stream the upstream breaks off, goes silent on past the read timeout, or closes with neither `[DONE]` nor a finish reason ends with one SSE error event (`"type": "obleth_gateway_error"`, `"code": 502`) and then an aborted response. OpenAI's SDKs raise it as an `APIError`. It used to end with `fi

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changed in v2.3.0
chunks.text:
Read this too when you upgrade from v2.2.x. There is nothing to do before upgrading from v2.2.x: no new required values or Secret keys, and every schema change is additive.

**Applied at startup.**

- Postgres migrations `0036` and `0037`: [rejected request fields](/docs/models/model-registry#rejected-request-fields) on `models`, and a `kind` on the job table so a mesh job is only found through `/v1/meshes`. Video jobs written before `0037` are read as videos.
- ClickHouse columns on `usage`: `key_name`, `tenant_name` and `streamed`, added in place. Rows the older version spilled to its WAL replay with empty names and `streamed = false`.

**Behaviour that needs no action:**

- First-token time is recorded only for replies streamed to the client. A buffered reply has none (`0`) in the ledger, Request logs and `obleth_ttft_ms`, so a model mostly called without streaming shows far fewer first-token samples, and a lower median, than before. Older rows keep their values.
- Calls through `/mcp/<server>` appear in Request logs as `mcp` rows with no tokens or cost, so reports that count every `usage` row count them too.
- A deleted key or team keeps its name on its past requests.
- [Energy per model](/docs/sharing/energy-accounting) and rejected request fields change nothing until you configure them.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changed in v2.4.0
chunks.text:
There is nothing to do before upgrading from v2.3.x: no new required values or Secret keys, and the schema change is additive, so old and new pods run side by side. Coming from v2.2.x, also read the v2.3.0 section below.

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migration `0038`: a `session_affinity` column on `models`, `{}` for every existing model, so every model follows the gateway default, which is off.

**Turn session affinity on after the rollout.** [Session affinity](/docs/how-it-works/fairshare-engine#session-affinity) holds slots that only v2.4.0 knows how to hand over and free. Leave it off, gateway-wide and on every model, until every replica runs v2.4.0; with it off, v2.3.x and v2.4.0 replicas share slots as before.

**Behaviour that needs no action:**

- [Derived session ids](/docs/clients/conversations-and-sessions) change once for conversations whose system prompt and first user message together were longer than 8 KiB. Those conversations get ids of their own instead of sharing one, so Request logs group them apart and `session_hash` routing spreads them across endpoints. Shorter openings hash exactly as before.
- OpenAI's `prompt_cache_key` is read as a session id when the request has no `session_id` or `metadata.session_id`.
- Every `auto` response carries `x-obleth-auto-model`, and `obleth_auto_routes_total` counts `auto` picks. [Keeping a conversation on its model](/docs/routing/auto-model-routing#keep-a-conversation-on-its-model) is off until you turn it on in Set

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changed in v2.5.0
chunks.text:
Coming from v2.4.x: the schema changes are additive, so old and new pods run side by side, but four changes can turn away traffic that v2.4.x served. Read **Check before upgrading** first. Coming from v2.3.x, also read the v2.4.0 section below.

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migrations `0039` (`batch_files`, `batch_file_chunks`, `batches`, `batch_items`) and `0040` (`mcp_servers.allowed_tenants`, empty for every existing server).

**Check before upgrading:**

- **MCP servers called directly close.** A server is now reached at `/mcp/<name>` only by keys of the tenants named for it, and every existing server starts with none, so direct calls answer 403 until you name them. Right after the upgrade, open each server that clients call directly and pick their tenants under **Tenants that can call it directly**, or `PUT /api/v1/mcp-servers/{id}` with `allowed_tenants`. Tools granted to models are not affected. See [MCP gateway](/docs/clients/mcp-gateway).
- **Only inference endpoints are forwarded.** A request on any other path or method, such as a model server's own management or file routes, now answers 404 `unknown endpoint`, even when its body names a model, and no setting opens it again. The forwarded endpoints are listed in [Data-plane routes](/docs/reference/data-plane-routes#path-handling).
- **Dashboard sign-in no longer joins accounts by email.** A first sign-in through an identity provider whose email already belongs to a dashboard account, such as the break-glass admi

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changed in v2.6.0
chunks.text:
This release is about [deployments on Slurm](/docs/deployments/overview); an install that doesn't run any sees no difference. Coming from v2.4.x, also read the v2.5.0 section below.

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migration `0041` adds columns for the new deployment settings and replica details, and allows a replica count of 0. It also replaces the environment values kept in existing launch-history rows with `(hidden)`; the variable names stay. That can't be undone, and nothing reads those values back: launch history is only shown and used to suggest settings.

**Check before upgrading:**

- **Upgrade the gateway and the provisioner together.** The provisioner reads the new fields and calls the new routes. The dashboard works with an older gateway, but without pauses, surge-first restarts or **Apply to running replicas**.
- **Recipes are checked more strictly.** A recipe with an unknown key, an undeclared `{{token}}`, a fixed `--port` or no `$OBLETH_SERVING_PORT`, or an `#SBATCH` line obleth can't send shows as invalid with the reason, including recipes saved in the database. Fix them on the Recipes tab; see [Deployment recipes](/docs/deployments/deployment-recipes).
- **Mint a long-lived Slurm token.** A plain `scontrol token` lasts 30 minutes; use `scontrol token lifespan=2592000` (30 days). The Slurm connection now shows when its token expires.

**Behaviour that changes on its own:**

- **The API version is `auto`.** A connection saved with the old default `v0.0.40` keep

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changes in v2.10.0
chunks.text:
The client address can be found past a chain of proxies, you can name your own networks under **Settings › Networks**, and Key access is now a tab of **Reports** (old `/key-access` links still work). No migrations. Coming from v2.8.x or earlier, also read the sections below.

**Optional after upgrading.** If requests reach obleth through a tunnel and then a proxy (for example Cloudflare to `cloudflared` to HAProxy), list those proxies in `OBLETH_TRUSTED_PROXIES` so each request is recorded at the client's address rather than the tunnel's; see [Where the client address comes from](/docs/sharing/key-networks#where-the-client-address-comes-from). With the default list nothing changes. A proxy that sets a header holding only the client's address can be named in `OBLETH_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADER` (Helm `obleth.clientAddress.addressHeader`).

**Check before listing your proxies.** Keys limited to certain networks are checked against the client address. A key whose allowed networks include a tunnel's address, because that is what earlier reports showed, will refuse its requests through the tunnel once the tunnel is listed. Replace those entries with the clients' real networks first.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changes in v2.11.0
chunks.text:
Keys can be limited to countries as well as networks, named networks hold several ranges and can be marked **Ours**, a key's allowed networks pick named networks as chips, and refused uses can be read for many keys at once. See [Where keys work](/docs/sharing/key-networks). Coming from v2.9.x or earlier, also read the sections below.

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migration `0045` adds `api_keys.allowed_countries`, empty for every existing key.

**During the rollout.** Resolved keys are cached under a new Redis namespace, `obleth:key3:`, and each replica writes every active key there from Postgres when it starts. Delete `obleth:key2:*` once no older replica runs.

**After upgrading:**

- **Save your named networks.** A list saved by an older release is read as before, with rows that share a name merged into one network. Group the ranges by network under **Settings › Networks**, tick **Ours** on your own, and save. Once saved in the new shape, an older release shows the list without names, so save only after every replica runs v2.11.0.
- **Countries need your proxies listed.** A key limited to certain countries admits a request by its country only when `OBLETH_TRUSTED_PROXIES` is set to your proxies' own addresses; with the default list the country is recorded but admits nothing. Settings › Networks says which applies.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changes in v2.12.0
chunks.text:
The gateway has an object store: one S3-compatible bucket, turned on with one setting. [Batches](/docs/clients/batches) keep their files and answers there instead of Postgres, and are off until it is on. An input file is deleted as soon as its batch ends, and a batch with its answers 24 hours after it ends (it was 30 days after creation). Coming from v2.10.x or earlier, also read the sections below.

**Before upgrading.** Make a bucket and a key that may put, get and delete objects in it, and name them:

- Helm: `obleth.objectStorage.enabled: true`, `.bucket`, `.endpoint` for a store other than AWS S3, and `.existingSecret`, a Secret with `OBLETH_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `OBLETH_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.
- Compose: `OBLETH_S3_BUCKET`, `OBLETH_S3_ENDPOINT`, `OBLETH_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `OBLETH_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`.

Without the object store, `/v1/files` and `/v1/batches` answer `404` after the upgrade. `obleth.batches.enabled` (`OBLETH_BATCHES`) is gone, and `obleth.batches.retentionDays` is now `obleth.batches.retention`, a duration such as `72h` (`OBLETH_BATCH_RETENTION`; the old variable is still read when the new one is unset).

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migration `0046` removes the batches and files stored the old way, whose content was in Postgres where the new gateway does not read it, drops `batch_file_chunks`, and frees their space at once. Let running batches finish and download their output and error files before upgrading.

**During the rollout.** Once the first

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changes in v2.7.0
chunks.text:
This release is about [keys](/docs/sharing/key-networks): a new key format, keys limited to certain networks, a client address on every request, and keys that use only spare capacity. Coming from v2.5.x, also read the v2.6.0 section below.

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migrations `0042` (`api_keys.background`) and `0043` (`api_keys.allowed_networks`, empty for every existing key). ClickHouse gains the `usage` columns `client_ip`, `client_network`, `client_country` and `user_agent`, and the tables `key_rejections` and `key_country_seen`.

**Check before upgrading:**

- **Route `obl_` keys first.** New keys start with `obl_` and 56 hex characters. A reverse proxy that picks a backend by the shape of the key, for example to split traffic between obleth and another gateway, must accept that shape before the upgrade, or every key made afterwards goes to the wrong backend. Existing `sk_` keys don't change.
- **Check which proxies are trusted.** In v2.7.0 the client address is the last `X-Forwarded-For` entry when the peer is in `OBLETH_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (Helm `obleth.clientAddress.trustedProxies`), by default any private or loopback address. If clients can reach the gateway directly from a private network, list only your proxies. From v2.10.0, a list you set is also read past every listed proxy. See [Where keys work](/docs/sharing/key-networks#where-the-client-address-comes-from).
- **Remove client-sent country headers** at every proxy in front of the gateway that doesn't set `C

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changes in v2.8.0
chunks.text:
You choose what new keys start with, under **Settings › Keys** (see [API keys](/docs/sharing/tenants-and-keys)). The built-in prefix is `sk` again. Coming from v2.6.x or earlier, also read the v2.7.0 section below.

**Applied at startup.** Postgres migration `0044` saves `obl` as the key prefix when the instance already has `obl_` keys and no prefix is saved, so an upgrade from v2.7.0 keeps making `obl_` keys. Any other instance makes `sk_` keys with 56 hex characters.

**Check before upgrading.** A reverse proxy that picks a backend by the shape of the key must accept the shape new keys will have: `sk_` and 56 hex characters, unless the instance keeps `obl`. To match any prefix, older `sk_` keys included, use `[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,2}_[0-9a-f]{48}([0-9a-f]{8})?`.

chunks.title: Upgrades
chunks.heading: What changes in v2.9.0
chunks.text: A dashboard page, **Access › Key Access**, shows where each key is used from and the requests that were refused. Since v2.10.0 it is the **Key access** tab of **Reports** (see [A tour of the dashboard](/docs/dashboard/control-plane#reports)). No migrations, and nothing to check before upgrading. Coming from v2.7.x or earlier, also read the sections below.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: API keys
chunks.text:
| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Format | A prefix, `_`, then 56 lowercase hex characters: 48 random (24 bytes), then an 8-character CRC-32 of everything before it. The prefix is `sk` (59 characters in all) unless set under Settings › Keys or `OBLETH_KEY_PREFIX`: 1 to 3 lowercase letters or digits, starting with a letter. v2.7.0 made `obl_` keys; keys made before it are `sk_` and 48 hex characters with no checksum. All keep working |
| Checksum | A key of that shape, with any prefix, whose checksum doesn't match is refused with `401` before any lookup, as is any malformed `obl_` key |
| Display prefix (`key_prefix`) | First 18 characters |
| Stored hash (`key_hash`) | SHA-256 hex of the full key; with a pepper, SHA-256 of key, a zero byte, then the pepper |
| Secret shown | Once, in the create response |
| Redis entry | `obleth:key3:<hash>` |
| Allowed networks | Optional; a request from outside them gets `403` `ip_not_allowed`. See [Where keys work](/docs/sharing/key-networks) |

The pepper is `OBLETH_API_KEY_PEPPER` (Helm `obleth.apiKeyPepper`). With it
set, a copy of the database alone cannot confirm guessed keys. Adding,
changing or removing it invalidates every secret key issued before, and a
restored backup authenticates only on a gateway with the same pepper.

Each key has a `kind`:

| `kind` | Credential | Created by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | The key, `sk_…` or the prefix chosen under Settings › Keys | The dashboard or `POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/keys` |
|

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Dashboard
chunks.text:
The dashboard has its own sign-in; browsers never see the admin token. Its
server calls the Management API with `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN`.

| Part | How it works |
| --- | --- |
| Accounts and sessions | [Dashboard auth tables](/docs/reference/postgres-schema) in Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`) |
| Session signing | `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, or `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` when unset; at least 32 characters |
| Break-glass admin | Seeded from `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` (at least 8 characters) when no active admin exists |
| Email sign-up | Closed; accounts come from SSO or the break-glass admin |
| SSO | `OIDC_PROVIDERS` ([Dashboard SSO](/docs/dashboard/dashboard-sso)) |
| Allowed origins | `BETTER_AUTH_URL` plus `TRUSTED_ORIGINS` (comma-separated; `*` trusts all) |
| Roles | `admin`, or `user` (a portal user tied to one tenant) |

A new SSO user starts as a pending `user` until an admin activates them on the
Users page. The seed never re-promotes an existing account with the same email.
No admin can demote or deactivate themselves or the last active admin.

The gateway hashes the presented key and looks it up in an in-process cache
(entries live up to 300 seconds; [invalidation messages](/docs/reference/redis-layout)
drop them early), then in Redis. The data plane does not read Postgres to
authenticate a secret key. The Management API writes Redis on every change,
and the gateway re-pushes keys from Postgres at start, every
`OBLETH_REDIS_REWARM_SECS`, and after a Redis

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Data plane
chunks.text:
Every request on port `8080` except `GET /health` carries a credential, an API
key or an identity token, in one of two headers:

| Header | Form | Used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <credential>` | First; the `Bearer ` prefix is case-sensitive |
| `x-api-key` | `<credential>` | When there is no `Authorization: Bearer` header |

Anthropic clients send `x-api-key` by default; set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to a
gateway key. The gateway strips both headers before forwarding to a model
backend. The MCP gateway (`/mcp/{server}`) and `/v1/verdicts` accept the same
credentials.

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "example-model", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}'
```

When `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` is set, a credential that starts with `eyJ`, has
exactly two dots and is at most 8 KiB is verified as an identity token.
Anything else is looked up as an API key.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Failure responses
chunks.text:
| Condition | Status | `message` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No credential | `401` | `missing bearer token` |
| Unknown or deleted API key | `401` | `invalid api key` |
| Identity token failed verification, or unknown subject with `jit_provision: false` | `401` | `invalid token` |
| Redis error during the key or identity lookup | `503` | `authentication backend unavailable` |
| Verified token, but its identity key could not be created | `503` | `identity provisioning unavailable` |
| Key disabled | `403` | `api key disabled` |
| Key used from outside its allowed networks | `403` | `This API key can't be used from <address>. Its owner limited it to certain networks.` (code `ip_not_allowed`) |
| Tenant not active | `403` | `tenant is not active` |
| Tenant start time not reached | `403` | `tenant is not active yet` |
| Tenant expired | `403` | `tenant access has expired` |
| Outside the tenant's weekly schedule | `403` | `tenant is outside its scheduled access window` |

Errors use `{"error": {"message": "…", "type": "obleth_gateway_error"}}`.
`/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` return the same statuses in the
Anthropic error envelope, with `missing api key` when no credential is sent.
A Redis error during the lookup returns `503`, not `401`, so a Redis outage
does not look like a revoked key to clients.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Identity tokens (JWT)
chunks.text:
With `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` set, the data plane accepts short-lived JWT access
tokens from the issuers it lists. A verified token maps to an identity key,
an `api_keys` row with `kind = 'identity'` and `key_hash` =
`jwt:` + SHA-256 of issuer, a zero byte, and subject. From then on the request
is handled like one with a secret key.

| Check | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Issuer | `iss` must equal a configured `issuer` |
| Audience | `aud` must contain the issuer's `audience` |
| Required claims | `exp`, `aud`, `iss`; the header needs a `kid` |
| Time | `exp`, `nbf` and `iat` checked with 60 s of clock skew |
| Signature | Against the issuer's JWKS, with an allowed algorithm |
| Subject | The `subject_claim` must be a non-empty string |

`OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` is a JSON array read once at start. A parse error, a
duplicate issuer, a disallowed algorithm, or a failed discovery fetch stops the
gateway from starting. Each entry takes:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issuer` | required | `http(s)` URL; exact match on `iss` |
| `audience` | required | Exact match on `aud` |
| `tenant` | required | Tenant name for new identity keys; created if missing |
| `jwks_url` | `jwks_uri` from `<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` | Where signing keys are fetched |
| `algorithms` | `["RS256", "ES256"]` | Any of `RS256`, `RS384`, `RS512`, `PS256`, `PS384`, `PS512`, `ES256`, `ES384`, `EdDSA` |
| `subject_claim` | `sub` | Claim that identifies the user |
| `device_claim` | unset

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.heading: Management API
chunks.text:
Every request on port `9180` carries the admin token:

```bash
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/tenants \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

The whole header must equal `Bearer <OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN>`, compared in
constant time; `x-api-key` is not accepted. A missing or wrong token returns
`401` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`. The token has no default: the gateway
does not start without it. It grants full access, with no per-user roles.
`GET /api/v1/health`, `GET /api/v1/version` and `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
need no token. Keep port `9180` private ([Security](/docs/operate/security)).

To add dashboard sign-in through your IdP, see

chunks.title: ClickHouse usage
chunks.heading: Data retention
chunks.text:
A background worker runs at startup and then hourly, dropping whole `usage`
day partitions older than the retention window. The window defaults to
`OBLETH_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` (180) and is set live with
`PUT /api/v1/settings/usage-retention`; stored values are clamped to 1 to 36500
days. `POST /api/v1/usage/compact` prunes now. `usage_daily` is never pruned,
and you need no ClickHouse `TTL` on `usage`.

| Table | Rows go | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | Day partitions past the retention window | `OBLETH_USAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` or the setting above |
| `usage_daily`, `key_country_seen` | Never | |
| `spans` | 14 days after `start_ms` | Fixed |
| `key_rejections` | 35 days after `ts_ms` | Fixed |
| `key_network_seen` | `OBLETH_CLIENT_IP_RETENTION_DAYS` after `last_seen_ms` | Client address retention |
| Columns `client_ip`, `client_network`, `user_agent` | `OBLETH_CLIENT_IP_RETENTION_DAYS` after the row | Client address retention |

A changed client address retention is applied at the next start with one
`ALTER` per table, which ClickHouse carries out on stored rows in the
background (a mutation per table).

chunks.title: ClickHouse usage
chunks.heading: Key tables
chunks.text:
`key_rejections` holds requests refused for a turned-off key (`reason`
`disabled`) or from outside a key's networks (`ip_not_allowed`): `ts_ms`,
`key_id`, `key_name`, `tenant_id`, `tenant_name`, `reason`, `client_ip`,
`client_country`, `user_agent`, `path` and `count`. Each replica writes at most
one row per key, address and reason every 10 seconds and counts the rest. It is
partitioned by month, and a table `TTL` with `ttl_only_drop_parts = 1` drops a
part once all its rows are 35 days old (above the longest window a reader asks
for, 31 days); `client_ip` and `user_agent` are cleared after
`OBLETH_CLIENT_IP_RETENTION_DAYS`. A table made before the TTL gets it at the
next start (marker `key_rejections_ttl_v1` in `usage_meta`).

`key_country_seen` (an `AggregatingMergeTree` fed by the materialized view
`key_country_seen_mv` from `usage`) keeps `first_seen_ms` and `last_seen_ms`
for each key and country, so the first time a key was seen from a country
outlives usage pruning. `key_network_seen` (fed the same way by
`key_network_seen_mv`) keeps them for each key and `client_network`; a row goes
`OBLETH_CLIENT_IP_RETENTION_DAYS` after its `last_seen_ms`, and a changed
retention moves its TTL as it moves the address columns'. It is seeded once
from the ledger when first created (marker `key_network_seen_v1` in
`usage_meta`). Read them through
[`/usage/key-sources` and `/usage/key-rejections`](/docs/reference/management-api#where-keys-are-used).

chunks.title: ClickHouse usage
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The gateway inserts usage rows and never updates them. Each replica buffers
rows and trace spans and inserts them every
`OBLETH_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS` (default 5000, from 100 to 60000), or at
once when 500 are waiting, so a request reaches Request logs up to that long
after it ends. It creates its tables at startup, and adds missing columns and
indexes, in the database named by `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_DB` (default `obleth`).

| Table | Engine | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage` | `MergeTree` | One row per request, pruned to the retention window |
| `usage_daily` | `SummingMergeTree` | Daily rollup of `usage`, never pruned |
| `usage_daily_mv` | Materialized view | Feeds `usage_daily` from new `usage` rows |
| `usage_meta` | `ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at)` | Internal markers for one-time schema work |
| `spans` | `MergeTree` | Per-request timing spans, kept 14 days |
| `key_rejections` | `MergeTree` | Refused key uses, kept 35 days |

chunks.title: ClickHouse usage
chunks.heading: Useful queries
chunks.text:
Add `AND request_type NOT IN ('health_probe', 'benchmark')` to match what the
dashboard and Management API report.

Tokens by tenant, last 24 hours:

```sql
SELECT tenant_id,
       sum(input_tokens)  AS input_tokens,
       sum(output_tokens) AS output_tokens,
       count()            AS requests
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) * 1000
  AND request_type NOT IN ('health_probe', 'benchmark')
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY output_tokens DESC;
```

Cache hit rate by model:

```sql
SELECT model,
       countIf(cache_status = 'hit') AS hits,
       round(countIf(cache_status = 'hit') / count() * 100, 1) AS hit_pct
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR) * 1000
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY hits DESC;
```

Latency percentiles, last hour:

```sql
SELECT quantile(0.50)(ttft_ms)  AS p50_ttft_ms,
       quantile(0.95)(ttft_ms)  AS p95_ttft_ms,
       quantile(0.95)(total_ms) AS p95_total_ms
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR) * 1000
  AND status_code < 400;
```

Last use per key:

```sql
SELECT key_id,
       max(ts_ms)                 AS last_used_ms,
       argMax(model, ts_ms)       AS last_model,
       argMax(status_code, ts_ms) AS last_status_code,
       count()                    AS requests
FROM obleth.usage
WHERE ts_ms >= toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY) * 1000
GROUP BY key_id
ORDER BY requests DESC;
```

chunks.title: ClickHouse usage
chunks.heading: WAL and replay
chunks.text:
When ClickHouse is unavailable, including at boot, usage rows spill to a local
write-ahead log whatever `OBLETH_FAIL_OPEN` says. Spill segments are JSON-lines
files in `<OBLETH_WAL_PATH>.segments/` (default path
`./obleth-telemetry.wal`), rotated at 1 MiB or 60 seconds. When ClickHouse
answers, the gateway applies the schema and replays segments in order, one
checkpointed batch at a time with backoff.

- Spill stops at 256 MiB or 1,024 segments; past that, rows are dropped and
  counted in [`obleth_telemetry_rows_lost_total`](/docs/reference/prometheus-metrics).
  The in-memory buffer holds 10,000 rows; a full buffer also drops.
- A corrupt line moves to `<file>.corrupt` and the rest of the file replays.
- Each batch carries an `insert_deduplication_token` from its request ids, and
  `usage` and `usage_daily` set `non_replicated_deduplication_window = 10000`,
  so a replayed batch that had already committed is discarded, not counted
  twice.
- The Helm chart sets `OBLETH_WAL_PATH` to `/var/lib/obleth/telemetry.wal` on
  a per-pod `emptyDir`: spilled rows survive a container restart but not pod
  deletion.

chunks.title: Data-plane routes
chunks.heading: Authentication
chunks.text:
The credential comes from `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, or from
`x-api-key` when there is no bearer token. It is an API key or, with identity
tokens configured, a JWT. See [Authentication](/docs/reference/authentication).

| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No credential | `401` | `missing bearer token` (`missing api key` on `/v1/messages`) |
| Unknown API key | `401` | `invalid api key` |
| JWT rejected | `401` | `invalid token` |
| Redis or identity backend unreachable | `503` | `authentication backend unavailable` |
| Verified JWT that cannot be mapped to a key | `503` | `identity provisioning unavailable` |
| Key disabled | `403` | `api key disabled` |
| Key used from outside its allowed networks | `403` | `This API key can't be used from <address>. Its owner limited it to certain networks.` (code `ip_not_allowed`) |
| Tenant not active | `403` | `tenant is not active` |
| Before the tenant's activation time | `403` | `tenant is not active yet` |
| After the tenant's expiry | `403` | `tenant access has expired` |
| Outside the tenant's weekly schedule | `403` | `tenant is outside its scheduled access window` |

chunks.heading: MCP gateway
chunks.text:
`/mcp/{server}` and its sub-paths take the data-plane credential and tenant
gate, admit only keys of the tenants the server is opened to, replace
`Authorization` with the server's stored `auth_header`, and reverse-proxy the
bodies unchanged, so streamable HTTP and SSE both work. The caller's cookies
and forwarded-address headers are not sent, and only the response headers MCP
uses come back.
Outcomes are counted in
[`obleth_mcp_requests_total`](/docs/reference/prometheus-metrics). See
[MCP gateway](/docs/clients/mcp-gateway).

| Condition | Status | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Path traversal in the sub-path | `400` | `invalid request path` |
| Bad credential, key or tenant | `401`, `403`, `503` | As in [Authentication](#authentication) |
| Server disabled | `403` | `mcp server is disabled` |
| Server not opened to the key's tenant | `403` | `this key's tenant may not use this mcp server` |
| Server not registered | `404` | `mcp server '<name>' is not registered` |
| Body over 16 MiB | `413` | `request body too large` |
| Over 600 calls a minute from one key to one server | `429` | `too many calls to this mcp server; try again shortly` |
| Upstream unreachable | `502` | `mcp upstream request failed` |

chunks.title: Data-plane routes
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The data plane listens on `OBLETH_PROXY_LISTEN` (default `0.0.0.0:8080`).
Every route except `/health` needs a credential.

chunks.title: Data-plane routes
chunks.heading: Path handling
chunks.text:
- **One spelling for every method.** Before anything looks at the path,
  repeated slashes collapse, a trailing slash is dropped and a repeated `/v1`
  prefix (`/v1/v1/…`) is read as one, whatever the method. For `POST`, the bare
  `/responses`, `/messages`, `/messages/count_tokens` and `/verdicts` map to
  their `/v1` forms. The request is then served like the canonical path, with
  translation, boons, guardrails and the job ownership checks.
- **Path traversal.** A `.` or `..` segment, a percent-escape of a letter, a
  digit, `-._~`, `/` or `\`, or a `%` that starts no escape, returns `400`
  `invalid request path` before authentication.
- **Only known endpoints are forwarded.** The gateway sends a request on to a
  model's upstream only when it is a `POST` to one of the inference endpoints
  above or a `GET` for model discovery (`/v1/models`, `/v1/models/{id}`,
  `/model/info`). Every other path and method returns `404` `unknown endpoint`
  and never reaches an upstream or the usage ledger, even when its body names a
  model. No setting opens other routes: a model server's own routes (stored
  completions, files, fine-tunes, management) are not reachable through the
  gateway.
- **Registered-model paths.** Every forwarded inference endpoint must name a
  registered model in `model` (the form field for multipart); a name the
  gateway does not have returns `404` and never reaches a default upstream. An alias is
  replaced by the canonical name before admission, budgets, cac

chunks.title: Data-plane routes
chunks.heading: Request pipeline
chunks.text:
1. Authenticate and gate the key and tenant.
2. Read the body (up to 64 MiB), resolve the model, and check its
   [lifecycle](/docs/models/model-lifecycle): a retired model is refused with
   `410` or answered by its replacement.
3. Refuse endpoints the tenant's [guardrails](/docs/routing/guardrails#what-is-scanned)
   cannot enforce, then run boons and the input guardrails. Guardrails also run
   under `x-obleth-boons: off`.
4. Check the response cache.
5. Take a slot in the model's pool, waiting up to `OBLETH_ADMISSION_TIMEOUT_SECS`
   (default 60).
6. Reserve the per-minute and term budgets in Redis.
7. Forward with the model's upstream headers and the endpoint's `api_key`,
   retrying and failing over as configured.
8. Stream the response back, reconcile the budgets and write the usage row.

A request that fails on every attempt, or that the gateway times out, is not
billed. From the moment a request goes to a model server, a client that
disconnects is billed its prompt, verdicts included. An upstream 4xx or 5xx
without a usage block records zero tokens. Images bill `n × cost_per_image`,
speech bills input characters × `cost_per_character`, and embeddings bill
prompt tokens.

chunks.title: Data-plane routes
chunks.heading: Route behaviour
chunks.text:
- **Model listing.** `GET /v1/models` answers from the registry without calling
  an upstream: every enabled model once, sorted by id, with `id`,
  `object: "model"`, `owned_by: "obleth"`, `model_type`, `mode`,
  `quantization`, `tags`, `aliases`, the model's own `supports_*` flags,
  `boons` and `boon_details` (whether each boon runs, and the helper model
  that does its work), and each variant as its own entry with `variant_of` and
  `description`. Staged and retired models and
  `search` models are left out; a deprecated entry adds `status` and its
  lifecycle fields. A request body is ignored. `GET /v1/models/{id}` returns
  the same entry for a name, alias or variant, including a retired model, and
  `404` for a staged model or one outside the tenant's allowlist.
  `/model/info` never returns `api_base` or `api_key`. See
  [Model registry](/docs/models/model-registry#get-modelinfo) and
  [Model lifecycle](/docs/models/model-lifecycle).
- **Multipart uploads.** Audio, image edits and variations, and a video create
  with a reference frame are parsed: `model` is swapped for the upstream name,
  text fields are scanned and billed like JSON (image `n`), and file parts are
  forwarded unscanned. A multipart request gets one attempt, never a retry. See
  [Images, audio and speech](/docs/clients/multi-modal-models).
- **Video jobs.** A create is billed `cost_per_video` once the job is recorded.
  Follow-ups go to the endpoint that holds the job, take no fairshare slot or
  budg

chunks.title: Data-plane routes
chunks.heading: When a stream is cut short
chunks.text:
A stream is cut when, before its last event, the upstream's connection breaks,
the upstream goes silent past `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS`, or a chat or
text completion stream closes with neither `[DONE]` nor a finish reason. The
client then gets one error event, and the response is aborted, with no finish
chunk, usage chunk or `[DONE]`:

```text
data: {"error":{"message":"upstream stream ended before the response was complete (after 47 s)","type":"obleth_gateway_error","code":502}}
```

The seconds count from the start of the upstream call. OpenAI's SDKs raise the
event as an `APIError`. Every stream ends a cut this way: one passed through
from the upstream, each turn of the [tool loop](/docs/boons/tool-loop)
(including a follow-up or final turn that can't be dispatched), and the
[speculation](/docs/boons/speculation) boon's continuation. The translated
Responses stream ends with `response.failed` instead, and the Messages stream
with an `error` event, each carrying the message.

A cut is recorded as `502` and billed for what reached the client: the usage
the upstream reported, else the streamed text at about 4 characters per token,
else nothing. It is never billed the `max_tokens` estimate. A connection the
upstream drops after `[DONE]` is not a cut.

An error event the upstream sends itself is forwarded once, and the gateway
adds no event of its own. The request is recorded under the error's status
(its `code` when that is an HTTP status, else `502`) and billed the s

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The stack runs obleth on one host for development, evaluation or staging. Run
every command from `deploy/docker/` so Compose loads `deploy/docker/.env`.
What each variable does, and how Compose sets it, is in
[Environment variables](/docs/reference/environment-variables).

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Profiles
chunks.text:
Core services always start. `.env.example` sets
`COMPOSE_PROFILES=benchmark,edge,observability`; leave it empty for the core
services only, or add one for a single command with
`docker compose --profile slurm up -d`.

| Profile | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| none (core) | `postgres`, `redis`, `clickhouse`, `obleth`, `control-plane` |
| `benchmark` | `benchmark-backend`, a model-free test upstream |
| `mock` | Same as `benchmark` |
| `edge` | `haproxy` on port 80 |
| `observability` | `prometheus`, `grafana`, `jaeger`, `postgres-exporter`, `redis-exporter` |
| `slurm` | `obleth-provisioner` |
| `compressor` | `compressor`, the prose-compression sidecar (about 600 MB model) |
| `sso-dev` | `dex`, a local OIDC provider for testing dashboard SSO |

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Required variables
chunks.text:
Compose stops with an error when any of these is unset or empty.
`.env.example` has development values for all of them; replace each before a
shared deployment.

| Variable | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `postgres`, `postgres-exporter`, and both database URLs |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | `redis`, `redis-exporter`, and `OBLETH_REDIS_URL` |
| `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` | `clickhouse` and the gateway |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` | `obleth`, `control-plane`, `obleth-provisioner` |
| `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` | `control-plane` break-glass admin, at least 8 characters |
| `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` | `control-plane`, also as `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`; at least 32 characters |
| `GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `grafana` (`observability` profile) |

```bash
openssl rand -hex 16       # POSTGRES_PASSWORD, REDIS_PASSWORD, CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
openssl rand -hex 32       # OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN, DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET
openssl rand -base64 32    # OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY (optional, recommended)
```

Paste the values into `.env`; Compose does not run commands there. Keep
`REDIS_PASSWORD` URL-safe, since it is placed in `redis://:PASSWORD@redis:6379`.
After changing `.env`, recreate the service, for example
`docker compose up -d obleth`.

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Standalone datastores
chunks.text:
`datastores.compose.yml` runs Postgres, Redis and ClickHouse on their own, as
a durable tier for a gateway that runs elsewhere (a Helm install with the
bundled datastores off, or a binary):

```bash
cd deploy/docker
cp datastores.env.example datastores.env   # change every password
docker compose --env-file datastores.env -f datastores.compose.yml up -d
```

The project is named `obleth-datastores` and uses the same images and volume
names. Ports publish on `BIND_ADDR` (default `127.0.0.1`): `5432`, `6379`,
`8123` and `9000`. Set it to a private interface address to reach them from
another host, behind a firewall. Redis runs with `--appendfsync everysec` and a
password. Point the gateway at it:

```bash
OBLETH_DATABASE_URL=postgres://obleth:POSTGRES_PASSWORD@DB_HOST:5432/obleth
OBLETH_REDIS_URL=redis://:REDIS_PASSWORD@DB_HOST:6379
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_URL=http://DB_HOST:8123
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_USER=obleth
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD=CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_DB=obleth
```

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Start the stack
chunks.text:
```bash
cd obleth-gateway/deploy/docker
cp .env.example .env          # then change every password and secret
docker compose up -d --build
```

`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` runs the published images from
`ghcr.io/thediymaker/obleth-gateway/` instead of building. Pin a release in
`.env`:

```bash
OBLETH_VERSION=v2.12.0
```

`OBLETH_VERSION` defaults to `latest`; `dev` tracks edge builds. It tags all
five images, the compression sidecar included; `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION` pins
the sidecar to another tag.

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Stop the stack
chunks.text:
```bash
docker compose down
```

`docker compose down -v` also deletes the `pgdata`, `redisdata` and `chdata`
volumes: every tenant, key, model and all usage history. Take a
[backup](/docs/operate/backup-restore) first.

`COMPRESSOR_CPUS` (default `4`) sets the container CPU quota and the
onnxruntime thread count. The scoring model is chosen when the image is built:
`COMPRESSOR_SOURCE` (`onnx`), `COMPRESSOR_MODEL_ID`
(`chopratejas/kompress-v2-base`) and `COMPRESSOR_ONNX_FILE`
(`onnx/kompress-fp32.onnx`). `onnx/kompress-int8-wo.onnx` needs half the
memory but scores about 30% slower, so keep fp32 unless memory is short. The gateway calls the sidecar only when
`OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_URL=http://compressor:8080` is set, and skips it when it
does not answer.

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Variables Compose does not forward
chunks.text:
The `obleth` service hardcodes these, so a value in `.env` has no effect:

| Variable | Fixed value |
| --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_GLOBAL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | `4096` |
| `OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | `32` |
| `OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_HISTORY_SECS` | `3600` |
| `OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_ALGORITHM` | `hierarchical` |
| `OBLETH_CAPACITY_DISCOVERY_NAMESPACES`, `OBLETH_CAPACITY_DEFAULT_SERVICE` | empty (the `kubernetes` source needs a pod) |
| `OBLETH_PROXY_LISTEN`, `OBLETH_ADMIN_LISTEN`, `OBLETH_METRICS_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:8080`, `0.0.0.0:9180`, `0.0.0.0:9091` |
| `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_URL` | `http://clickhouse:8123` |
| `RUST_LOG` | `info,obleth=debug` |

`OBLETH_UPSTREAM_POOL_IDLE_SECS`, `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_TCP_KEEPALIVE_SECS`,
`OBLETH_PORT_SPAN`, the batch settings other than `OBLETH_BATCH_RETENTION` and
`OBLETH_BATCH_MAX_SHARE`, and the provisioner's `OBLETH_PROVISIONER_*` variables other
than `RESTART_AFTER_FAILURES` are not passed, so their defaults apply.

To change any of them, override the service's `environment:` in a second file:

```yaml
# deploy/docker/compose.tuning.yml
services:
  obleth:
    environment:
      OBLETH_DEFAULT_MODEL_MAX_IN_FLIGHT: "64"
      OBLETH_FAIRSHARE_HISTORY_SECS: "7200"
```

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f compose.tuning.yml up -d obleth
```

Or set `COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:compose.tuning.yml` in `.env` (`;` on
Windows) so every command includes it.

The `obleth` service has `stop_grace_period: 345s`: the 300 s
`OBLETH_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECS

chunks.title: Docker Compose
chunks.heading: Volumes
chunks.text:
| Volume | Service | Mounted at | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pgdata` | `postgres` | `/var/lib/postgresql/data` | Configuration and sign-in tables |
| `redisdata` | `redis` | `/data` | AOF; rebuilt from Postgres if lost |
| `chdata` | `clickhouse` | `/var/lib/clickhouse` | Usage ledger and spans |

Read-only bind mounts supply `clickhouse/prometheus.xml` and
`clickhouse/system-logs.xml` (ClickHouse's own logs at `information` level,
with a week of its system log tables kept), `haproxy.cfg`,
`dex/config.docker.yaml`, `prometheus.yml` and the Grafana `provisioning` and
`dashboards` directories.

chunks.heading: Docker Compose host ports
chunks.text:
| Service | Container port | Host binding | Profile |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `obleth` data plane | `8080` | `8088` | core |
| `obleth` Management API | `9180` | `127.0.0.1:9180` | core |
| `obleth` metrics | `9091` | `127.0.0.1:9091` | core |

| `postgres` | `5432` | `127.0.0.1:5432` | core |
| `redis` | `6379` | `127.0.0.1:6379` | core |
| `clickhouse` HTTP, native | `8123`, `9000` | `127.0.0.1:8123`, `127.0.0.1:9000` | core |
| `benchmark-backend` | `8081` | `8081` | `benchmark` |
| `haproxy` | `80` | `80` | `edge` |

| `dex` | `5556` | `5556` | `sso-dev` |

A binding without an address listens on all host interfaces. These ports
reach only the Compose network: HAProxy `8404` (metrics and `/stats`), the
compressor's `8080`, ClickHouse `9363` (metrics), `postgres-exporter` `9187` and
`redis-exporter` `9121`.

chunks.title: Endpoints and ports
chunks.heading: HAProxy frontend
chunks.text:
The Compose `edge` profile runs HAProxy; the Helm chart does not.

| Port | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `80` | Round-robin to the obleth data plane on `8080` |
| `8404` | HAProxy `/metrics` and `/stats` (Compose network only) |

The shipped config is plaintext and assumes TLS ends in front of it. See
[HAProxy](/docs/reference/haproxy).

chunks.title: Endpoints and ports
chunks.heading: Health checks
chunks.text:
`GET /health` on the data plane and `GET /api/v1/health` on the Management API
need no token and return `ok`.

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/health          # data plane, Compose host port
curl http://localhost/health               # through HAProxy (edge profile)
curl http://localhost:9180/api/v1/health   # Management API
curl -s http://localhost:9091/metrics | head
```

A plain `cargo run` binds `8080` directly, so there the data plane is on
`localhost:8080`. `GET /v1/models` needs an API key, so use `/health` for
liveness probes.

chunks.title: Endpoints and ports
chunks.heading: Kubernetes service ports (Helm)
chunks.text:
Every Service is `ClusterIP`; `<release>` is the Helm release name.

| Service | Ports | Present when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<release>-obleth` | `proxy` `8080`, `admin` `9180`, `metrics` `9091` | always |
| `<release>-control-plane` | `3000` | `controlPlane.enabled` |
| `<release>-compressor` | `http` `8080` | `compressor.enabled` |
| `<release>-postgres` | `5432` | `postgres.enabled` |
| `<release>-redis` | `6379` | `redis.enabled` |
| `<release>-clickhouse` | `http` `8123`, `native` `9000` | `clickhouse.enabled` |
| `<release>-benchmark-backend` | `8081` | `benchmarkBackend.enabled` |

The optional Ingress routes to `ingress.servicePort` (`8080`, the data plane).
The ServiceMonitor scrapes the `metrics` port. The provisioner has no Service.

With `networkPolicy.enabled`, the chart allows only this inbound traffic:

| Target | Allowed from |
| --- | --- |
| obleth `8080`, `9091` | anywhere |
| obleth `9180` | control plane and provisioner pods |
| Postgres `5432` | obleth and control plane pods |
| Redis `6379`, ClickHouse `8123` and `9000` | obleth pods |

See [Helm values](/docs/reference/helm-values) for the settings.

chunks.title: Endpoints and ports
chunks.heading: obleth listeners
chunks.text:
The gateway binary opens three listeners.

| Listener | Default bind | Set with | Serves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data plane | `0.0.0.0:8080` | `OBLETH_PROXY_LISTEN` | Client API, `/mcp/…`, `/health` |
| Management API | `0.0.0.0:9180` | `OBLETH_ADMIN_LISTEN` | `/api/v1/…` |
| Metrics | `0.0.0.0:9091` | `OBLETH_METRICS_LISTEN` | `/metrics` |

The other components listen on: control plane `3000`, compression sidecar
`8080`, benchmark backend `8081` (`BENCHMARK_BACKEND_LISTEN`). The provisioner
has no listener. Routes are listed in
[Data-plane routes](/docs/reference/data-plane-routes) and
[Management API](/docs/reference/management-api).

chunks.title: Environment variables
chunks.heading: benchmark-backend
chunks.text:
The model-free OpenAI-compatible test upstream behind the `benchmark` Compose
profile, the Helm `benchmarkBackend` Deployment and
[obench](/docs/operate/benchmarks).

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:8081` | Bind address |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_TTFT_MS` | `20` | Simulated time to first token |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_TOKEN_MS` | `5` | Delay between tokens; Compose and Helm set `3` |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_DEFAULT_OUTPUT` | `64` | Output tokens when a request sets no `max_tokens` |
| `BENCHMARK_BACKEND_CONCURRENCY` | `10000` | Requests served at once before callers queue; Compose and Helm set `256` |

Each also accepts a `MOCK_` spelling (`MOCK_LISTEN`, `MOCK_TTFT_MS` and so on)
as a fallback.

chunks.title: Environment variables
chunks.heading: Compose-only variables
chunks.text:
Docker Compose reads these to fill in `docker-compose.yml`; no obleth binary
reads them. See [Docker Compose](/docs/reference/docker-compose).

| Variable | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPOSE_PROFILES` | `benchmark,edge,observability` in `.env.example` | Optional services to start |
| `OBLETH_VERSION` | `latest` | Image tag of the first-party images; `dev` tracks edge builds |
| `OBLETH_COMPRESSOR_VERSION` | `OBLETH_VERSION` | Image tag of the compression sidecar, when it should differ from the gateway's |

chunks.title: Environment variables
chunks.heading: obleth gateway
chunks.text:
The **Compose** column says how `deploy/docker/docker-compose.yml` sets each
variable:

- **`.env`**: forwarded from `deploy/docker/.env`. A value in brackets is the Compose default when it differs from the binary's.
- **fixed**: hardcoded in the Compose file, so a value in `.env` has no effect. See [variables Compose does not forward](/docs/reference/docker-compose#variables-compose-does-not-forward).
- **composed**: built from other `.env` values, such as `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
- **not set**: Compose does not pass it, so the default applies.

For the Helm value behind each variable, see [Helm values](/docs/reference/helm-values).

| Variable | Default | What it sets | Compose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_PROXY_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:8080` | Data-plane bind address | fixed |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:9180` | Management API bind address | fixed |
| `OBLETH_METRICS_LISTEN` | `0.0.0.0:9091` | Prometheus metrics bind address | fixed |
| `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:8081` | Upstream for models with no `api_base` | `.env` (`http://benchmark-backend:8081`) |
| `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `5` | Longest wait to open a new connection to a model server; past it the next endpoint is tried. `0` turns it off | `.env` (commented) |
| `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `300` | Wait for upstream response headers; a model's `request_timeout_secs` overrides it | `.env` |
| `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS` | the upstream timeout, at least `120` | Longest

chunks.title: Environment variables
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
obleth has no configuration file. Each process reads the environment once at
startup. Settings that change at runtime (routing, boons, alerts, energy, the
Slurm connection, retention) live in Postgres and are changed from the dashboard
or the [Management API](/docs/reference/management-api).

Boolean variables accept `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `yes`/`no` and `on`/`off`,
in any case. An unparseable number falls back to the default.

chunks.title: Environment variables
chunks.heading: Set by the platform
chunks.text:
The gateway also reads variables that the container runtime sets, not you:

- `HOSTNAME` names the replica in its Redis heartbeat, with a random suffix. Without it the gateway reads `/etc/hostname`.
- `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` and `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT` locate the API server for the `kubernetes` capacity source, with the pod's ServiceAccount token.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Health checks
chunks.text:
The shipped `check` is a TCP connect check. For an HTTP check, use the data
plane's `/health`, which needs no token and returns the body `ok`:

```nginx
backend obleth_pods
    option httpchk GET /health
    http-check expect string ok
    server obleth1 obleth:8080 check inter 5s fall 3 rise 2
```

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
HAProxy runs in the Compose stack under the `edge` profile, from the image
`haproxy:3.2`, with `deploy/docker/haproxy.cfg` mounted read-only. The Helm
chart does not deploy it; on Kubernetes the obleth Service and the chart's
optional Ingress fill the same role (see [Helm values](/docs/reference/helm-values)).

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Run it
chunks.text:
`.env.example` already lists `edge` in `COMPOSE_PROFILES`. Otherwise:

```bash
cd deploy/docker
docker compose --profile edge up -d
```

HAProxy publishes port `80` on the host and forwards to the obleth data plane.
Keep the Management API (`9180`) off HAProxy and on the internal network.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Shipped configuration
chunks.text:
`deploy/docker/haproxy.cfg`, with its comments removed:

```nginx
global
    log stdout format raw local0
    maxconn 50000

resolvers docker
    nameserver dns 127.0.0.11:53
    resolve_retries 3
    timeout resolve 1s
    timeout retry  1s
    hold valid 10s

defaults
    mode http
    log global
    option httplog
    timeout connect 5s
    timeout client  300s
    timeout server  300s
    option http-no-delay

frontend obleth_front
    bind *:80
    option forwardfor
    http-request del-header CF-IPCountry
    default_backend obleth_pods

backend obleth_pods
    balance roundrobin
    server obleth1 obleth:8080 check resolvers docker init-addr last,libc,none

frontend stats
    bind *:8404
    mode http
    http-request use-service prometheus-exporter if { path /metrics }
    stats enable
    stats uri /stats
    stats refresh 10s
    stats realm obleth\ stats
    stats auth ${HAPROXY_STATS_USER}:${HAPROXY_STATS_PASSWORD}
```

`option forwardfor` appends the client's address to `X-Forwarded-For`, which the gateway records and checks a key's allowed networks against, and a client-sent `CF-IPCountry` is dropped. Behind another proxy that terminates HTTP, have that proxy set the header and pass it on here unchanged; see [Where keys work](/docs/sharing/key-networks#where-the-client-address-comes-from).

The `docker` resolver re-resolves `obleth` through Docker's DNS, so a
recreated gateway container with a new IP is picked up. To balance across
several gateways, add a `serve

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Stats page
chunks.text:
The `stats` frontend on `8404` serves the Prometheus exporter at `/metrics`,
without a password so Prometheus can scrape it, and the stats UI at `/stats`
behind basic auth. Compose exposes `8404` to its own network only. Set the
sign-in in `deploy/docker/.env`; Compose falls back to `admin` / `admin`:

```bash
HAPROXY_STATS_USER=admin
HAPROXY_STATS_PASSWORD=...   # change the development value
```

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: Streaming
chunks.text:
Streamed responses (`text/event-stream`) must pass through unbuffered:

- `option http-no-delay` sends each chunk as it arrives.
- `timeout client` and `timeout server` (300 s) bound silence on a connection. A non-streaming request is silent until the model answers, so keep them at or above `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_SECS`.
- Do not turn on `compression`; it buffers responses.

chunks.title: HAProxy
chunks.heading: TLS termination
chunks.text:
The shipped frontend is plaintext, on the assumption that a load balancer in
front of it terminates TLS. To terminate TLS in HAProxy, put the certificate
and private key in one PEM file and change the frontend:

```nginx
frontend obleth_front
    bind *:443 ssl crt /etc/ssl/private/obleth.pem
    bind *:80
    http-request redirect scheme https unless { ssl_fc }
    default_backend obleth_pods
```

Then mount the file and publish `443` in a Compose override:

```yaml
services:
  haproxy:
    ports: ["80:80", "443:443"]
    volumes:
      - ./certs/obleth.pem:/etc/ssl/private/obleth.pem:ro
```

chunks.title: Helm values
chunks.heading: Overview
chunks.text:
The chart is published at `oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth`; chart
version and `appVersion` are both `2.4.0`.

```bash
helm install obleth oci://ghcr.io/thediymaker/charts/obleth \
  --version 2.4.0 \
  --namespace obleth --create-namespace \
  --set obleth.adminToken=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  --set postgres.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  --set redis.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  --set clickhouse.password=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  --set controlPlane.dashboardPassword='change-me-now' \
  --set controlPlane.dashboardSessionSecret=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
  -f my-values.yaml
```

`--set` values end up in shell history and the release record. In production,
create the Secrets yourself and name them in
[`existingSecret`](#pre-created-secrets-existingsecret). Upgrading from 1.x
changes the Secret keys; see [Upgrading from v1.x](/docs/operate/upgrade-from-v1).

chunks.title: Helm values
chunks.heading: Pre-created Secrets (`existingSecret`)
chunks.text:
When `obleth.existingSecret` names a Secret, the chart renders none of its own
and every pod reads that one. It must carry these keys:

| Key | Needed | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN` | Always | Gateway, dashboard, provisioner |
| `OBLETH_DATABASE_URL` | Always | Gateway |
| `OBLETH_REDIS_URL` | Always; with bundled Redis, `redis://:<REDIS_PASSWORD>@<release>-redis:6379` | Gateway |
| `OBLETH_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD` | Always (may be empty for an external ClickHouse without one) | Gateway; bundled ClickHouse |
| `OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | Always (may be empty) | Gateway |
| `OBLETH_API_KEY_PEPPER` | Always (may be empty) | Gateway |
| `OBLETH_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | Always (may be empty) | Gateway |
| `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` | Optional | Gateway |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `postgres.enabled` | Bundled Postgres |
| `REDIS_PASSWORD` | `redis.enabled` | Bundled Redis |

`controlPlane.existingSecret` works the same way for the dashboard and must
carry `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD`, `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (falls back to `DASHBOARD_SESSION_SECRET` when absent),
`BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `TRUSTED_ORIGINS`, `DASHBOARD_ADMIN_EMAIL` and
`OIDC_PROVIDERS`.

The gateway, Redis and ClickHouse pods carry a `checksum/secret` annotation, so
a change to the chart's Secret rolls them. With `existingSecret` the checksum
never changes: restart the Deployments yourself after editing the Secret. The
gateway reads `OBLETH_JWT_ISSUERS` only at start. Start from
[`va

if it contains `@`, `:`, `/`, `?`, `#`, `%` or whitespace. Use hex
(`openssl rand -hex 16`). The dashboard enforces the lengths itself:
`dashboardSessionSecret` must be at least 32 characters, and a
`dashboardPassword` under 8 characters is not seeded.

chunks.title: Helm values
chunks.heading: Security contexts (Pod Security Standard)
chunks.text:
| Value | Default | What it sets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `podSecurityContext` | `runAsNonRoot: true`, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault` | Pod security context |
| `securityContext` | `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, drop `ALL`, `runAsNonRoot: true` | Container security context; `readOnlyRootFilesystem` is opt-in |
| `networkPolicy.enabled` | `false` | NetworkPolicies below; needs a CNI that enforces them |

Both contexts apply to the gateway, dashboard, provisioner, compressor and
benchmark backend, and meet the Kubernetes
[restricted](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/#restricted)
standard. No UID is pinned (gateway runs as `10001`, dashboard as `1000`). The
bundled datastores are left out because their images manage their own users.

With `networkPolicy.enabled`, ingress is limited to:

| Target | Allowed from |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled Postgres `5432` | Gateway; dashboard when `controlPlane.enabled` |
| Bundled Redis `6379` | Gateway |
| Bundled ClickHouse `8123`, `9000` | Gateway |
| Gateway `8080` (data plane) | Any source |
| Gateway `9091` (metrics) | Any source |
| Gateway `9180` (Management API) | Dashboard and provisioner, when enabled |

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: API keys
chunks.text:
`POST /api/v1/tenants/{id}/keys` and `PUT /api/v1/keys/{id}` take the same
body. A field left out of `PUT` keeps its stored value, and `null` clears a
cap, a budget or a list, so a `PUT` can name only what it changes.

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required on create | Display name |
| `description` | `""` | |
| `budget_tokens`, `budget_cost_usd` | `null` | Key caps; `null` is uncapped |
| `budget_period` | `null` (`lifetime`) | `lifetime`, `monthly`, `term` |
| `budget_started_at` | now, when a cap is set | Start of the current term |
| `weight` | `100` | Share among the tenant's keys, minimum 1 |
| `max_in_flight` | `null` | The key's cap within each model pool, minimum 1 |
| `allowed_networks` | `[]` (any network) | CIDR ranges or single addresses, at most 64; a single address is stored as `/32` or `/128`. A request from elsewhere gets `403` `ip_not_allowed` |
| `allowed_countries` | `[]` | Two-letter country codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), at most 50, stored upper-case; `XX` or anything that isn't two letters is a `400` naming the entry. A request whose client country is listed is allowed even from outside `allowed_networks`, once `OBLETH_TRUSTED_PROXIES` is set; with both lists empty the key works from anywhere. See [Where keys work](/docs/sharing/key-networks#limit-a-key-to-certain-countries) |

Create returns `{"key": {…}, "secret": "sk_…"}`. The secret is its prefix (`sk_` unless
[chosen](/docs/sharing/tenants-and-keys) otherwise) plus 56
hex

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Backup
chunks.text:
A backup holds fairshare groups, tenants, keys (hashes only),
models, endpoints, MCP servers and every settings row, not knowledge
collections. Secrets are carried as stored; restore refuses a backup whose
`key_check` does not match the target's `OBLETH_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, warns on an
API-key pepper mismatch, and returns inserted and updated counts plus
`warnings`. See [Backup and restore](/docs/operate/backup-restore).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Batches
chunks.text:
Every tenant's [batches](/docs/clients/batches), for operators. Callers manage
their own through `/v1/batches` on the proxy port.

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches` | Batches across tenants, newest first; filters `status` (one status, or `active` for every unfinished one), `tenant_id`, `model`; pages with `limit` (50, at most 200) and `after` (a batch id) |
| `GET` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}` | One batch |
| `POST` | `/api/v1/batches/{id}/cancel` | Cancel a batch for its owner; audited as `cancel_batch` |

The list returns `data`, `has_more` and `counts`: batches by status across
every tenant, regardless of the filters. Each batch has `id`, `tenant_id`,
`tenant_name`, `key_id`, `key_name`, `model`, `endpoint`, `status`, `total`,
`completed`, `failed`, `completion_window`, `created_at`, `in_progress_at`,
`deadline_at`, `last_progress_at`, `finished_at`, `waiting` (no request has
finished for two minutes while some are left), `metadata` and `errors`.

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Conventions
chunks.text:
The gateway serves the Management API on the admin listener
(`OBLETH_ADMIN_LISTEN`, default `0.0.0.0:9180`). The dashboard uses the same
routes. Keep the port on a private network; see
[Security](/docs/operate/security).

| Topic | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Auth | `Authorization: Bearer <OBLETH_ADMIN_TOKEN>` on every route except the three public ones below; compared in constant time; wrong or missing is `401` |
| Body | JSON, `Content-Type: application/json` |
| Audit actor | Every write records an audit row; the actor is the `X-Obleth-Audit-Actor` header, default `admin` |
| Errors | `{"error": "<message>"}` with `400` invalid input or refused URL, `401`, `403` protected target (the reserved control-plane tenant), `404` unknown id (also a nested id under the wrong parent), `409` name conflict, `502` saved in Postgres but the Redis cache update failed (run `POST /api/v1/resync`) |
| Secrets | Write-only. Responses carry `api_key_set`, `auth_header_set`, `upstream_header_names`, `password_set`, `slack_webhook_set`, `jwt_set` instead. Omit a secret on update to keep it |
| Partial updates | Settings bodies: an omitted field keeps its stored value. Resource `PUT`s note their own rules below |
| Pagination | List routes return everything unless they page. `/keys` pages with `limit` + `after` (the last key's id); request logs with `before_ms` + `before_request_id`; the audit log with `before_id`. While rows past a page match, the response carries `x-obleth-truncated: true` (so do `/

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Daily usage rollup
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/usage/daily` reads the permanent rollup, so it covers dates the
raw ledger has dropped. It excludes benchmark traffic.

| Query param | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start_day`, `end_day` | 7 days ago, today | Inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `tenant_id`, `model` | unset | Filters |
| `key_id` | unset | One id or a comma-separated list |
| `group_by` | `day` | `day`, `tenant`, `key`, `model`, `key_model`, `day_tenant`, `day_model`, `day_key_model` |

Each row carries `ttft_requests`, the requests its first-token average is
taken over, so averages of several rows can be weighted by it. Days rolled up
before the count existed have `0` there and average over their answered
requests.

**Overview and stats.** `/overview/summary` returns `requests`, `tokens`, `input_tokens`,
`output_tokens`, `errors`, `platform_errors`, `cost`, `has_pricing`,
`p50_ttft_ms`, `avg_ttft_ms`, energy and CO2 totals, and `tenant_count`, `active_tenants`,
`model_count`, `enabled_models`, `key_count`. Unfiltered reads of it are
shared for up to 15 seconds per gateway replica, so the totals can be that
stale. `/overview` takes `since_ms`, `until_ms`, `bucket_ms` and
`include_internal` and returns `since_ms`, `until_ms` (the read's "now" when
open-ended), `previous_since_ms` (the previous window is as long as this one
and ends at `since_ms`), `bucket_ms`, `summary` and `previous` (each shaped
like `/overview/summary`), `series` (buckets over both windows, shaped like
`/usage/series`), `mod

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Failure classes
chunks.text:
Every failed request records a class and a reason. The class says whose
failure it was: the platform's, when the gateway or a model server could not
serve a valid request, or the client's, when the request could not be served
as sent. The reason is the model server's own error message, or the
gateway's, cut to 300 characters. It never holds request or answer text.

| Class | Side | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client_input` | client | Refused as sent: a bad field, a prompt over the context window, images to a text-only model |
| `client_cancel` | client | The client disconnected before the answer was complete (`499`) |
| `retired` | client | The model is retired (`410`) |
| `limit` | client | A rate limit or budget of the tenant or key |
| `capacity` | platform | No slot was free within the admission wait |
| `upstream_timeout` | platform | The model server did not answer in time |
| `upstream_error` | platform | The model server failed, or its answer stream broke off |
| `network` | platform | The model server could not be reached |
| `gateway` | platform | The gateway itself failed |

Rows written before v2.5.0 have no class of their own. Reads file them by
status code and admission decision: `499` client cancel, `410` retired, `429`
limit, a rejected `403` limit, a rejected `503` capacity, `504` upstream
timeout, any other `4xx` client input, any other `5xx` upstream error.

`GET /api/v1/usage/failures` returns `requests`, `failures` and
`platform_failures` for the fil

chunks.text:
`PUT` also takes `chunk_tokens` (400) and

chunks.heading: MCP servers
chunks.text:
A name is 1–64 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting
with a letter or digit. `PUT` requires `upstream_url` and takes
`auth_header` (omit or `""` keeps it), `clear_auth: true` to remove it,
`enabled`, and `name` (a rename carries into every model's grant). Responses
show `auth_header_set`. See [MCP gateway](/docs/clients/mcp-gateway).

chunks.title: Management API
chunks.heading: Model capacity and auto-tune
chunks.text:
`PUT …/capacity-mode` takes `capacity_mode` plus the optional
`capacity_source`, `capacity_namespace`, `capacity_service`,
`per_replica_max_in_flight` and `capacity_headroom`, with the same rules as
`PUT /api/v1/models/{id}`. A `discovered` write the gateway cannot discover is
refused with `400`. See [Pool sizes](/docs/models/pool-sizes).

`POST …/autotune` probes the upstream directly (bypassing admission) for
`chat` and `embedding` models, within 60 s and 20000 requests, and writes
nothing. See [Capacity auto-tune](/docs/models/capacity-autotune).

| Field | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workload` | `chat` | `chat` or `coding` prompt shape |
| `latency_headroom` | `4.0` | Multiple of single-request p99 that marks the knee; 1.5–20 |
| `replicas` | unset | Sizes the ramp ceiling at 32 per replica |
| `max_concurrency` | `64` | Explicit ceiling, overrides `replicas`; at most 512 |

The report has `recommended_max_in_flight`, `knee_reason`
(`latency_degraded`, `plateau`, `max_concurrency`, `no_data`),
`baseline_p99_ms`, `latency_ceiling_ms`, `recommended_throughput_rps`, and
per-step results. `…/autotune/apply` takes `{"max_in_flight": N}`.

| --- | --- |

| `…/reliability` | `request_timeout_secs` (`null` uses `OBLETH_UPSTREAM_

chunks.heading: Per-key usage summary
chunks.text:
`GET /api/v1/keys/{id}/usage` returns `last_used_ms`, `last_model`,

| `include_internal` | `false` | Include health probes and benchmark traffic |

A key with no traffic returns zeros and `last_used_ms: 0`.
